#1976. Glasner made to wait for first win as Trafford thwarts Forest

James Trafford became the record signing for a British goalkeeper this summer and he is already proving invaluable for Leeds United.

Signed from Manchester City for an initial £40m in August, Trafford has made an outstanding start and frustrated Nottingham Forest twice in four days.

The England international secured his second successive clean sheet in this City Ground sequel to underline why Leeds moved to eclipse the previous record for Jordan Pickford.

“England’s No 1” was a frequent chant from the travelling Leeds fans and although it may take some time for him to dislodge Pickford as the country’s first-choice, he is loving life at his new club.

Trafford produced a number of fine saves and goals from Daniel James and James Justin secured a comfortable Carabao Cup second-round victory for Leeds, who also won here in the league on Saturday.

Dan James has put Leeds ahead against Nottingham Forest 💥 pic.twitter.com/BdiYMXFJ5h

Leeds manager Daniel Farke said: “He has the potential to be one of the best goalkeepers in the Premier League and that is why Thomas Tuchel has picked him for England.

“I like his natural confidence and aura, he knows that he’s good and he will be outstanding one day.

“He has major chances to be under the spotlight and we are very pleased with him so far.”

Forest manager Oliver Glasner will be pleased to see the back of Leeds. He was appointed by Forest for the primary reason of winning trophies after successful tenures with Crystal Palace and Eintracht Frankfurt, but this particular avenue is now closed for this season.

Four-time League Cup winners, Forest endured a difficult evening following the pre-match news that they have agreed a £45m deal with Chelsea for striker Liam Delap.

Forest have established a reputation for noisy transfer windows but are determined to focus on quality over quantity this year. With Delap to undergo a medical on Wednesday, Forest will then focus on signing a new right wing-back before the deadline.

Newcastle’s Jacob Murphy has been discussed, though a move is now regarded as unlikely. There are understood to be other targets under consideration.

Glasner has insisted he does not want Forest to panic, and it remains to be seen whether they do spring into life on the final day. He said: “I am not a magician or the messiah and we cannot ignore the reality that Leeds are ahead of us at the moment.

“For nine months last season we were fighting relegation, so the players know it is going to take a lot of work. I know exactly what we have to change and that is what we will do.

“We are responsible and made so many mistakes. Maybe we needed this result. At the moment we are far away from what we want but we will get there.”

This was a more open game than the attritional encounter from last weekend, as Trafford was forced into a fine early save to prevent Ola Aina’s cross from arcing into the top corner.

Yet both teams were frequently making mistakes and providing masterclasses in how to misplace passes, frustrating their respective managers in the technical area.

The most impressive moment of the first-half came from Leeds centre-back Joe Rodon, racing back into position to deny Chris Wood from close range. Rodon celebrated the tackle as if it were a 30-yard screamer.

It was always likely to be a mistake which proved the pivotal moment, and Arnaud Kalimuendo’s poor header cost the home team in the 50th minute.

Kalimuendo’s error presented Sean Longstaff with space to run into and his pass found James, who beat Matz Sels with a clinical finish.

“Can we play you every week?” was the inevitable chant from the travelling Leeds supporters.

Forest’s fans were becoming twitchy and Trafford produced another save to frustrate Wood from eight yards after a break down the right from Kalimuendo.

Glasner responded by making a quadruple substitution on the hour, yet Leeds remained dangerous and added a second goal 15 minutes from time when Justin bundled home after a goalmouth scramble.

Ethan Ampadu's long throw causes CHAOS in the Forest box as Leeds go 2-0 up! pic.twitter.com/CtGDDIaRNp

You can catch the draw for the next stage of the League Cup on Sky Sports Main Event tomorrow night after the conclusion of Preston North End vs Everton.

Nottingham Forest have agreed a club-record deal worth £45m for Chelsea forward Liam Delap.

Delap has been deemed surplus to requirements at Stamford Bridge, and while the clubs were in talks over an initial loan deal, they have now struck a permanent agreement for the striker.

The 23-year-old​ only signed for Chelsea in a £30m deal from Ipswich Town 12 months ago​ ​and is scheduled for a medical on Wednesday​. He will become Forest’s most expensive signing with the deal eclipsing the £37.5m they paid for Omari Hutchinson last summer.

Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a new forward and Delap was a long-term target for the Austrian since his time as Crystal Palace head coach.

Delap held talks with Forest last year over a potential move, and was also understood to have spoken with Glasner while he was at Palace.

Speaking to ITV after the win, Rodon said: “I thought we were a bit sharper going forward, maybe a bit naive in the first half. I thought we had a lot of good chances maybe could have scored a couple of goals but we know it’s a difficult place to come and overall very happy to keep a clean sheet and win the game.”

Of his last-ditch tackle in the first half, he added: “We love it, as defenders it’s as good as a goal. I’m delighted, [keeping] clean sheets is my job and overall I got it right in the end.”

"There's a healthy arrogance about Leeds""Farke has gone from strength to strength"Izzy Christiansen and Jobi McAnuff praise the impact of Daniel Farke at Leeds 📈 pic.twitter.com/fgzLWRk3U2

"It's a bit soon to say Wembley!" 😅James Justin and Dan James react to Leeds progressing into round three of the Carabao Cup 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/m81C6eJT7C

And that is it. Two home defeats by Leeds in less than 80 hours for Forest. Glasner will have much to ponder with a daunting trip to Anfield coming up on Saturday. All smiles for Farke’s side.

A look at a third for Leeds. Aaronson drives forward before setting Wilson who in turn lays on a first-time pass to Calvert-Lewin. The forward attempts to take his shot first time but can’t get the requisite power on the ball to beat Sels.

A pitch invader makes a brief appearance on the turf but is swiftly ushered away.

There is a late chance for Forest. Hutchinson’s cross is helped on by Dominguez but that touch inadvertently takes the ball away from Ndoye at the back post.

Forest fans are filing out of the exits and who can blame them?

That just about sums up Forest’s night. Dominguez stands over a free-kick from a dangerous area and, with the box loaded with their most imposing aerial threats, the midfielder sends the ball well over their heads and out for a goal-kick. So poor.

Calvert-Lewin is now on for Nmecha. Not really the striker Forest defenders would want to see at this stage of the game.

Another set-piece, this time a Stach corner, is barely dealt with by Forest.

There’s a shout for a handball at the other end as Ndoye spears a cross into the body of Elvedi, but the referee rightly waves the appeals away.

The “oles” ring out from the away end as Leeds string a series of passes together in the corner right in front of it. Forest are looking rather helpless here.

Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 2 (Justin) Ampadu launches a throw-in from the right but has to reload as the referee notices some pushing in the box. His next attempt is far too loopy but causes Forest all sorts of trouble, bouncing and bobbling, and coming all the way through a thicket of limbs to Nmecha at the far post. Williams attempts to keep the ball out from a prone position on the goalline under pressure from Justin, who gets the final touch as the ball is bundled over the line.

It's messy but Leeds won't care! 😁Forest fail to deal with the throw-in and Nmecha is there to bundle it in...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/oV46fs5RmP

Jair goes into the book after catching Ampadu in full flight. He never had a prayer of reaching that ball.

The resulting free-kick lands to Amapadu himself in the box, but his effort is deflected behind for a corner which is not up to much.

Goalscorer James is taken off for Bogle, who will offer more mettle down Leeds’ right side as Forest search for an equaliser in the closing stages.

Stach has only been on the field for a matter of seconds but comes within a few inches of scoring. Wilson does well on the edge of the box before laying the ball to Stach whose curled effort grazes the outside of the side-netting.

Longstaff’s final contribution to this game is a foul and yellow card as he spreads his legs wide to stop Ndoye breaking away through the middle.

He is replaced by Wilson, as Tanaka and Okafaor also make way, for Stach and Aaronson.

There’s plenty more endeavour down Forest’s new-look left side. Hudson Odoi scampers down that flank before cutting inside, and while he’s unable to fashion a chance the intent is correct.

The substitutions appear to have breathed life into this Forest side. Murillo picks out Dominguez charging forward and Trafford does well to tip the midfielder’s effort behind. The resulting corner comes to nothing.

Glasner resolves he has seen enough and rings the changes. Diomande, Aina, Jesus and Kalimuendo are replaced by Murillo, Netz, Ndoye and Hudson Odoi.

Okafor shows off his dancing feet in the Forest box, pulling off a few stepovers before the ball comes to Ampadu on the edge of the area but his strike is dragged wide.

Chances at both ends! Kalimuendo plays a wonderful ball into the box for Wood to sweep home but Trafford springs into action and makes a stunning save.

Leeds go up the other end, Okafor profiting from a diversionary run from centre-back Elvedi but cannot find the target and double Forest’s lead.

End-to-end football! ⚡️First Wood, then Okafor - just 19 seconds between the two chances 😮#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/TGQmtwLNwE

Leeds are ahead and the inevitable chant from the away supporters is “can we play you every week?”

This is of course their second meeting in four days and Leeds are on course to record the double.

Forest’s fans are starting to get a little twitchy.

Dan James puts Leeds United in front! ⚽️Tidy finish from the Welshman... #EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/GzWg6zLGLm

Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 1 (James) We finally have a breakthrough. Kalimuendo gives the ball up cheaply in the middle of the park and Longstaff is there to pick up the pieces, darting infield before laying on a perfectly weighted for James to gallop on to, take a touch and sweep beyond Sels. The winger has been Leeds’ biggest threat and deserves that goal.

James finds space down the right - again - and his cross is closed down and deflected behind for a corner.

Longstaff’s floated delivery is tipped away by Sels, but it turns out that the ball went out before coming in so a Forest goal kick is awarded.

A lovely rendition of Mull of Kintyre precedes a short blast of the referee’s whistle and we’re back under way...

Schlager goes into the book instantly for grabbing a handful of Tanaka’s shirt as the Japan international attempted to escape his clutches.

This hasn’t been much of an improvement from Saturday.

Both teams are producing masterclasses in how to misplace passes. Oliver Glasner and Daniel Farke have spent much of the first half looking very frustrated.

James Trafford must be feeling very comfortable and confident of a second successive clean sheet after joining from Manchester City.

Let’s hope for an improvement in the second-half.

Should the scores remain level after 90 minutes, we will go straight to penalties. There’s still a half to play of course, but Forest’s League Cup shoot-out record should be a source of confidence having won seven from eight.

What a tackle from Joe Rodon! 💥#EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/p5GkzSFEoZ

James wins the ball on the halfway line and feeds Okafor down the left. He attempts a deft through-ball into a thicket of bodies but it comes to nothing.

Leeds circulate the ball, working the ball from side to side but there is nowhere near enough movement in front of the ball-player for any meaningful forward passes to be played.

And, quite aptly, the referee blows up at three seconds past 45 minutes. Certainly not a half for the books.

Another half-chance for Forest! Milenkovic lands on a second ball off a deep free-kick but he cannot keep his strike down. A classic centre-half’s effort if you will.

Ampadu comes over to the left to fire in a long throw-in. Sels comes steaming out of his goal and fumbles the ball but is awarded a free-kick after Muharemovic makes contact. Looked very minimal in all fairness.

Oof, a good chance for Aina! Williams’ cross from the left comes all the way through to his opposite wing-back, but Aina’s half-volley sails over. A cracking contact, though.

Elvedi and Muharemovic look to be astute buys from Leeds’ perspective. Both assured at the back and the latter especially is confident progressing the ball.

Just as I type that Forest threaten with a ball over the top, but Justin nips in to take the ball away from Wood.

Another decent opening for Leeds after a Forest turnover. Nmecha strides through the middle but Milenkovic is in position to ensure his run comes to nothing.

What a tackle! Kalimuendo bursts through the middle after Leeds cede possession in a dangerous position. The winger plays in Wood who looks to be through on goal but Rodon comes out of nowhere to telescope a limb and stop the forward in his tracks. Fantastic defensive work from the Welshman.

Nmecha attempts to break beyond the halfway line but is stymied by a swarm of Forest players. He demands a foul from the referee who is not interested in the least.

It’s then Okafor’s turn to put in a dangerous cross from the left, but Nmecha cannot get to it.

Tanaka becomes the first man to go into the book. The ball gets away from him and Jesus puts body between man and ball smartly to win the foul.

Tanaka is now dropping into the back line to allow Leeds’ defenders the licence to get wider and higher. Forest will need to be wary of their opponents’ numerical advantage down the flanks.

The game has reached something of a holding pattern as both sides resolve to slow things down, at least temporarily. Forest have settled into a slightly deeper block.

Sensing an opportunity, Ampadu spins in a glorious through-ball between centre-back and full-back for James to gallop on to. He hits the by-line and cuts back to Longstaff, but the midfielder can’t beat Sels. A good chance that probably should have been converted.

A good chance goes begging! 🫣Longstaff is free for Leeds but fires it straight at Sels...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/0UJdfSDQ6w

Tanaka then turns provider, winning possession in Forest’s half before playing in Longstaff, whose cross-cum-shot does not threaten Sels’ goal.

Both sides have physical, quick out-balls, which has made for a frenetic encounter thus far. James rasps in another fierce cross from the right after another sweeping Leeds move, but Nmecha cannot get there and Tanaka fires well over on the follow-up.

Aina’s throw-in, this time from the left, is flicked on to Jesus at the back post and while the forward is able to direct the ball goalwards there is Justin on the line to clear the ball to safety.

Chance! Dominguez slides in Aina down the right channel and the full-back’s mishit cross has Trafford scrambling. He palms the ball behind for a corner, which is headed away for a Forest throw-in on the far side.

Leeds are enjoying a spell of possession here, Tanaka and Longstaff peeling off into the wide areas to collect the ball and disrupt Forest’s mid-block out-of-possession structure. The hosts are more than happy for Leeds to circulate the ball in front of their first line of pressure as, for the second time tonight, Trafford boots it out into touch.

Dominguez stands up a smart cross to the far post where Aina is waiting to head back across goal. Trafford backpedals into Kalimuendo and the referee awards Leeds a free-kick.

Wonderful touch there early in the game from none other than Oliver Glasner.

Forest’s head coach perfectly trapped a high ball as it landed towards him in the technical area.

James shows off his speed for the first time tonight, accelerating down the right before fizzing a dangerous ball into the six-yard box but Forest clear their lines.

Sels goes long to Wood (feels like the right play given his attributes), James lands on the second ball but can only boot the ball into row Z to jeers from the home fans.

Aina launches a long throw-in from the right and it’s headed behind for a corner. Trafford punches the inswinging delivery away and Williams’ effort from the edge of the box sails well over.

Forest are in their red home shirts, kicking from left to right. Leeds are in their yellow away number. Same set-up as the weekend.

Players and mascots walk on to the City Ground turf. A place in the League Cup third round on the line.

The first pre-match question put to Glasner by ITV was in relation to the reported £45m club-record deal for Chelsea forward Liam Delap. He responded: “I can tell everybody that he doesn’t play today. Everything else we shall see in the next days.”

Oliver Glasner breaks his silence on Nottingham Forest's record signing, Liam Delap 🚨He speaks to @gabrielclarke05 ahead of Forest's Carabao Cup tie against Leeds 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/8DlWMIzVS9

Reflecting on Saturday’s defeat by Leeds in his programme notes, Glasner wrote: “I saw plenty of encouraging signs from the team on Saturday and I felt we were a lot closer to scoring than we were conceding, especially in the second half. Unfortunately, the small margins were not on our side.

“I thought our defence looked comfortable, but there is still work to be done and the more the players get used to the system we’re operating, the more we’ll see that work come to fruition in competitive matches.

“We have recovered well and will be ready to give our all this evening.”

Previewing tonight’s League Cup match, Leeds head coach Daniel Farke said: “Our league win is good for our mood and confidence, but this is a ‘do or die’ cup game. Both teams will be motivated to progress, so I expect a tight game. It will be difficult to win on the road again against a tough opponent.”

When asked what winning a first trophy of his managerial career would mean to him, Farke added: “Well, we weren’t too far away last season. Overall, I would say my form in cup competitions hasn’t been too bad during my career. I’m a big believer in these competitions, I like the ‘do or die’ mentality. I would never say no to another good cup run.”

The hosts’ kits tonight will include Carabao Cup sleeve patches with the number four on them, in recognition of the club’s League Cup triumphs in 1978, 1979, 1989 and 1990.

This is Forest and Leeds Part 2, just four days after they clashed in the Premier League.

Daniel Farke ruined the Oliver Glasner welcoming party on Saturday with a 1-0 smash-and-grab victory at the death.

Both managers have gone relatively strong for this tie, with only a sprinkling of debuts.

Ousmane Diomande, the £34m signing from Sporting, makes his first appearance while there is a first start for Xaver Schlager.

Leeds have given a debut to Switzerland defender Nico Elvedi.

Nottingham Forest Sels; Diomande, Jair, Milenkovic; Aina, Schlager, Dominguez, Williams; Jesus, Kalimuendo; Wood

Subs Victor, Murillo, Abbott, Netz, Hutchinson, Ndoye, McAtee, Sangare, Hudson Odoi

The big breaking news is that Forest are smashing their club record to sign Chelsea forward Liam Delap for £45m.

Delap will undergo a medical at Forest on Wednesday with the deal potentially rising to £50m after add-ons.

It eclipses the previous transfer record of £37.5m for winger Omari Hutchinson.

Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a new centre-forward this summer and Delap ticks pretty much every box for him.

Farke makes six changes to the complement that started against Forest in the league on Saturday.

📋 Your #LUFC XI... pic.twitter.com/XuUzwwkmfi

Wood makes Glasner’s XI while summer acquisitions Diomande and Schlager are handed their first competitive Forest starts.

Our @Carabao_Cup XI this evening. 📋 pic.twitter.com/Wv918WJScj

Welcome to live coverage of the Carabao Cup second-round match between Nottingham Forest and Leeds United. This will be the sides’ second meeting at the City Ground in four days after Anton Stach’s late free-kick decided an attritional contest on the Premier League’s opening weekend. Forest’s new head coach Oliver Glasner is something of a cup specialist, though, with FA Cup, Europa League and Conference League titles to his name and he will relish the opportunity to right the wrongs of Saturday in front of the Forest faithful.

The Austrian is Forest’s fifth head coach in less than 12 months and he will look to arrest the churn by bringing to the City Ground the success he enjoyed with Crystal Palace. During pre-season, the Austrian moulded Forest into his preferred 3-4-3 shape, placing summer acquisition Ousmane Diomande alongside the existing central-defensive partnership of Murillo and Nikola Milenković. Here, Diomande gets his Forest debut and Glasner brings in talisman Chris Wood from the start.

Daniel Farke will have been delighted to see his Leeds side continue their excellent form in pre-season – which included victories over Liverpool, Red Bull Leipzig and Augsburg – into the season proper. Although Leeds arrive at the City Ground shorn of attacking options Wilfried Gnonto, Noah Okafor and Mateo Joseph through injury, Farke still shuffles the pack in the forward positions with this weekend’s visit of Brentford to Elland Road in mind.

#1975. GdS: Predicted XIs for Genoa vs. Milan – Pavlovic out but starters return

Ruben Amorim will bring back the big guns for tomorrow’s starting eleven against Genoa, although Strahinja Pavlovic remains at risk of missing the game.

Thursday’s performance against Ferencvaros was a very poor one and it’s safe to say that some of the deputies didn’t take their chances. As such, with Genoa up next on Sunday afternoon, Amorim is set to revert to the usual eleven.

The only problem is that Pavlovic is still struggling with shoulder discomfort, which could keep him on the sidelines. Amorim has previously highlighted how important the Serbian’s mentality is, but a return won’t be rushed.

According to Gazzetta dello Sport this morning, the likes of Mike Maignan (suspended last time out), Mario Gila, Pervis Estupinan, Luka Modric, Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic will come into the eleven.

Six changes, in other words, which could turn into seven if Pavlovic does make it back in time. As for Genoa, there are some familiar faces as Stephan El Shaarawy and Lorenzo Colombo are both expected to start the game. Another former Milan man will also be on the bench, namely Junior Messias.

#1974. Is Jobe Bellingham England's next big thing who shares his older brother's 'X-Factor' - or a 'problem child' whose dad blows up at his bosses? Inside the rise of the 21-year-old after first call-up

Published: 09:16 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 16:31 EST, 6 November 2026

For years, Jobe Bellingham has been in the shadows of his older brother Jude.

Now, for the first time since they were children, the duo are poised to perform on the same stage. Only this time it won't be under the lampposts of Stourbridge, but the floodlights at Wembley.

Jobe, 21, has been called up to England's senior squad for the first time and is often described in similar terms to his elder sibling: relentlessly ambitious, focused, and a quick learner who is wise beyond his years.

'You have to have an X-Factor and Jobe does,' said Regis Le Bris, his old manager at Sunderland.

That X-Factor appears to run in the Bellingham blood. Earlier this week Jude was unveiled as the new underwear heart-throb for Calvin Klein, channelling his inner David Beckham in a smouldering photoshoot. No pressure, Jobe.

Their main difference on the pitch is that Jobe, while versatile, tends to occupy a deeper-lying role in midfield – and that actually increases the chances of Thomas Tuchel fielding them together. There is every chance that, against Croatia or Spain next week, we will see just the fourth pair of brothers to feature for England since the Second World War.

Jude and Jobe Bellingham's dream of playing for England together may finally come true

The duo grew up playing together and both joined the Birmingham City academy (Instagram: judebellingham)

The duo visited the Spanish Grand Prix in September with matching shirts and haircuts

They share a close relationship and in September were VIP guests of McLaren for the Spanish Grand Prix, posing for photographs in matching blue shirts and identical haircuts, a mischievous double act.

If you were a few pints deep in the Formula One hospitality area, you'd be forgiven for thinking they were the same bloke – especially when their footballing trajectories are so similar.

Jobe began his career at Birmingham City, like Jude, before moving to Sunderland and now Borussia Dortmund, where his brother also played. Jobe, who is two years younger than his superstar brother, is now in his second full season with the Westphalia giants.

He has previously admitted his trepidation at following in Jude's footsteps, once telling the German club's in-house media channel: 'I was biased against joining Borussia Dortmund for a very long time.

'I had anxieties, fears, and you want to be your own man. But I don't think I should let those stop me from making the right decision.'

The comparisons are inevitable, though, when you share the same name and your potential also happens to be through the ceiling. It is a theme Jobe will simply have to contend with wherever he roams.

In Dortmund's 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich on Saturday, the resemblance was striking as he delivered a standout performance – even having the ball in the back of the net, though his goal was ruled out for a Carney Chukwuemeka foul.

At one stage, Bellingham backheeled the ball over Aleksandar Pavlovic, won the ball back off Dayot Upamecano, drifted past Pavlovic with a skill that left him on one knee, and drove about 30 yards towards goal before firing a shot just over the bar.

They would be just the fourth pair of brother to play for England since the Second World War

Jude and Jobe are pictured together at a Louis Vuitton Paris Fashion Week show in 2023

In that ten-second flash, he displayed the sort of tenacity, ingenuity, and swagger which we have come to associate with Jude.

While not as brazen on the surface as Jude, Jobe perhaps gets some of his confidence from their father Mark.

The brothers were introduced to football by their dad, a retired police sergeant who also scored 700 goals in non-league.

Raising his sons in the West Midlands alongside their mother Denise, Mark gave them tips on how to improve and how to deal with the pressures of football. Jude even describes his father as his first footballing hero.

The crackerjack duo have always competed to see who can be the most precocious. Jude became Birmingham City's youngest-ever player when he debuted for them in 2019. When Jobe made his bow for them in 2022, he did so just 69 days older.

He earned his move to Sunderland after just 26 games and was a hit on Wearside. In his second campaign, he won the Championship Young Player of the Season award and helped them to promotion via the play-offs.

Manager Le Bris was breathless in his praise. 'There are many [qualities], there is a long list,' he said. 'Probably his ambition is one of the first ideas I have when I think about Jobe.

'He is very ambitious but this ambition is not naive. It is connected with what he is doing every day in training and every game on the pitch.

Jude pictured with his brother Jobe, father Mark, and mother Denise upon signing for Borussia Dortmund in 2020

'He has many good qualities as a footballer. He is very powerful and he understands the game very well. He is really interested in the game and, because of that, he is able to improve with experiences. He can learn very quickly.

'He is older than his age. He has more maturity. He is like an exception in the sport. It is not easy to play at the level he is doing so at his age, but he is doing so well.'

In the summer of 2025, Dortmund got on the blower. They were willing to pay £31million – more than they had for Jude – and put him straight in the squad for the Club World Cup. Dortmund's UK scout is Daniel Dodds, the brother of Mike, who had worked with Jobe in Birmingham's academy and at Sunderland.

'I think he can go to the very top,' Mike told the Northern Echo in 2023. 'Both brothers have a very similar mindset in terms of their relentlessness in their pursuit of where they want to get to.'

Despite the extravagant projections, Jobe's time in Germany's industrial belt has not been entirely smooth. Often he has been left to simmer on the bench, unable to nail down a regular starting spot.

In his first Klassiker experience, he came on only to lose the ball and have Michael Olise's shot deflect in off him. One report described him as a man who looked 'completely stripped of confidence'.

On the opening day of last season against St Pauli, he was hauled off at the break, leading to his father going ballistic and allegedly confronting sporting director Sebastian Kehl. That put Jobe in an awkward spot. He was also sent off for a professional foul against Freiburg.

Amid his struggles to adapt to the Bundesliga, he has copped criticism off the ferocious pundit Dietmar Hamann, who blasted him as a 'problem child' in a column for Sky Sport. 'Young, expensive and, so far, not even half as good as Jude Bellingham,' seethed the former Liverpool midfielder.

Jobe has become a more regular starter since the turn of the year and, in any case, has always been highly thought of in English football circles.

Jobe helped Sunderland to promotion from the Championship - manager Regis Le Bris said he had the 'X-factor'

Lee Carsley made Jobe his captain for the Under-21s and waxed lyrical about him: 'I think he will be an all-round box-to-box player. He can be creative, score goals. I still feel he can score more goals.

'His shooting is excellent, especially in training. He can link and receive in tight areas.'

Carsley added: 'He’s a good example to the rest of the group, the way he conducts himself on and off the pitch, the way he prepares, the influence he has on the rest of the team.

'He’s a player who can grow into that role. We just assume that players understand leadership and how that works. It will be good to add another string to his bow and keep improving his game.'

After his U21s debut against Spain in Cadiz, he was ambushed by people who wanted signatures... on their Real Madrid shirts. It was opportune and distasteful, but reflected the bigger picture: the name Bellingham is associated with Jude.

Now Jobe's moment has come. Tuchel picked him partly because of Carsley jabbering on with praise in his ear over recent months. The noise around him has become unavoidable and, with Alex Scott injured and Myles Lewis-Skelly suspended for the first game, the Three Lions are light in midfield.

'To play with my brother for England that would be the biggest dream of my life. Nothing would even get close to that,' Jude said in 2024. That may soon be a reality.

“I would like to see Luke Graham get more minutes for Scotland given his form,” said Phillips. “When you talk about players going away on international duty, I've been there. However, while the former boasts more international experience with 13 caps, Phillips insists that Graham’s form should put him ahead of others when the team face off with North Macedonia at Hampden Park.

“Luke Graham was probably frustrated in the last camp,” Phillips told Best Betting Sites. “All he can do is go away and play well for his club, and he's done that. Hopefully now he's knocking on the manager's door and asking for more minutes. So yeah, I would say he deserves a bit more of a chance, and hopefully after these next games he certainly gets that, because he's more than capable of playing at that level.”

#1972. Eastbourne United wallop Wick to keep league ambitions on track

A rare 4-3 home reversal against Roffey had not helped the mood, the near hurricane conditions rendering the match a spectacle rather than a competition.

On United went to Horsham YM last Tuesday. Sam Scott was suspended and Zach Robitaille made his full debut as United steamrollered hapless YM.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

It could have been different; in a first half in which Alieu Secka only touched the ball from a couple of back passes, it was a solitary Ryan Blunt goal that separated the teams, and YM might be forgiven for thinking that it would be contained.

There was none of that as Anthony Storey’s half-time talk obviously did the trick. In a second half that once again they dominated, United added four more.

Blunt added a second with a left-foot drive before Callum Barlow rose at an impossible angle to head the third.

The YM keeper had earned his corn all match, and made an exceptional save from Ball before Blunt completed his hat-trick. Baran Kartal joined from the bench, and managed to sneak one home to make it 5-0, and to be fair, YM were fortunate that it was just five.

United knew that was more of a test coming on Saturday as they travelled to Wick.

Wick are having work done at Crabtree Park and are playing home games at Bognor’s Nyewood Lane ground. United were on a bit of a high and were unchanged but it was a very different start – as in the first minute at Hassocks, a defensive mix-up led to Wick taking the lead.

The difference here was that United bounced straight back. Joe Overy grabbed the first of his brace with eight minutes on the clock, and Wick were immediately looking more fragile. Overy and Jones were penetrating time and again, but without a real meaningful attempt.

Brett Patton, dominant as ever in midfield, took it upon himself to do the job, picking the ball up in the midfield, pushing straight through the defence and rounding the full-back like he wasn’t there, smashing home to make it 2-1. Patton does not score many, but when he does, it’s usually goal of the month.

Wick hearts were broken and it was an inevitable second half as United piled up the goal attempts. Blunt made it 3-1 just after the break before Overy’s excellent effort was pushed out by the keeper to Jorge Nones to sidefoot home from 12 yards.

The rout was completed minutes later as Overy scored his second, making it 5-2 before a raft of changes as surely the strongest bench in the league released Ball, Stone, James Hull, Gander and Kartal into the action.

The win meant United stayed a strong second in the table, and United have now scored 60 goals in their first 17 matches.

It’s a long campaign, but it’s not far off the halfway mark now, and United must be considered serious contenders for the league and certainly for the play-offs. Next up on Saturday it’s Little Common, so often a thorn in United’s side, at the Oval Arena.

#1971. Why England will privately regret missing out on Scott McTominay - 'he wasn't saying anything about them'

When Jose Mourinho first alerted Alex McLeish to the possibility of securing Scott McTominay's international allegiance, little could he have imagined the midfielder would become one of Scotland's most influential players.

The former Manchester United manager wanted to know if McLeish was aware McTominay was eligible to represent Scotland. That conversation proved the starting point of an international career that has become hugely beneficial to the national team.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

McTominay's return to the Scotland squad earlier this week, following heart surgery, for the final Nations League double-header against North Macedonia and Switzerland represents a major boost for new head coach Sebastien Pocognoli, who will welcome the availability of such a talismanic figure early in his tenure.

For McLeish, however, the Napoli midfielder's inclusion rekindles memories of the international tug-of-war that could so easily have ended in England's favour.

The Three Lions were also interested in 2018, but Scotland were determined not to miss out on a promising young talent at Old Trafford. McLeish recalls travelling south during the ‘Beast from the East’ to watch McTominay first-hand, where his physical presence and technical ability immediately caught his attention.

However, it was McTominay’s emphatic response when offered the chance to pull on the dark blue jersey that ultimately settled the matter.

“Everyone will read this and be saying ‘there he goes again!’ But it was amazing to get him,” McLeish admitted. “Word was in the air about Scott and Jose phoned me and said ‘you know this boy can play for Scotland?’ And I said, ‘I do now!’ I then organised to go down to see him. He was still just a kid, quite raw. But he had the physique, speed and skill on the ball. He was good in the air and also with the ball at his feet that made it a no-brainer.

“The only problem we faced was that England were in the frame as well. But when I said to Scott, ‘I'd love you to play for Scotland,’ he said ‘That's the only nation I want to play for.’ And all of a sudden we had a brand new young superstar.”

The value of that decision has become increasingly apparent. McTominay has developed into a commanding international presence, combining physical strength, technical ability and a natural eye for goal from midfield.

Initially deployed in defensive positions, including centre-back, he has since made his mark further up the pitch, with his ability to drive through midfield and time his runs into the penalty area becoming a major asset.

“It's incredible how he's grown and grown,” McLeish said. “In the first few games he was just trying to feel his way into the international scene. But Scott gave everything from that first call-up. He's played in just about every position in the team down the years. He was in the back four at one stage. But he's mainly operated in the middle of the field and he's a real threat in the box and moving from middle to front.

“The way he runs with the ball is just superb because he really knows what he's doing. He's got massive confidence and I hope that a lot of young Scottish players coming into the game can take inspiration from what Scott has done.”

There is also the question of whether England have been left to rue a missed opportunity. Having come through Manchester United's academy, McTominay was a player England could realistically have pursued. However, Scotland's willingness to offer him a clear international pathway was ultimately rewarded.

McLeish suspects the decision will not have gone unnoticed south of the border. stating: “They have such a massive pot to pick from in England. But I'm sure that privately, in some of their chats behind the scenes, they will have said ‘we should have got McTominay.’ But he chose Scotland. He wanted to come. He wasn't saying anything about England at all. And that was the best news I could have got in that era of rebuild.”

McTominay's return provides a timely boost for Pocognoli as he looks to put his own stamp on the national team. Having an established performer of his calibre available will be a significant advantage for the new head coach.

McLeish knows the difficulties of international management when key players are unavailable. During his own spell in charge, he recalls travelling to Kazakhstan with several important members of his squad missing.

“It'll be a massive relief for the manager to get Scott back into the squad. You always want your best players available. I remember back in my day, going out there and we were held in a bit of limbo. So for Pocognoli to get players into his team of that level will be massive for him. It could make a huge difference for Scotland.”

#1969. ‘Without doubt’ – Lack of physicality major reason behind Crawley Town’s league position, says interim boss

Having been at the club for three weeks, Blackwell has had ample opportunity to assess the Reds squad.

And the former Leeds and Sheffield United once again highlighted Crawley’s deficiencies.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

He said: “We are neither technical or physical. We are not a totally technical side or a totally physical side.

“We brought Ben [Heneghan] in who is a 6ft 3 centre half, we brought Connor [Wickham] at 6ft 2 up front – we need some more physicality.

“In central midfield we have nobody above 5ft 8. You look at the games against Tranmere and against Oldham, they were physically towering above us yet we’ve shown we have the capabilities to fight.

“It’s not all about just having big boys, it’s about having the desire and the fight to make sure that you win your battle.”

Blackwell also reiterated his concerns surrounding the club’s recruitment.

He added: “Once again, I question the recruitment. If you have six people in midfield and the tallest is 5ft 10 and three are 5ft 8, how do you deal with a 6ft, 6ft 2 midfield player?

“We’ve got to look at balancing the physical and technical side. I see us at the moment being half of one and half of the other and it’s not working.”

League Two is an extremely physical division – and Blackwell admitted the Reds were being ‘bullied’ by opposition teams.

He said: “Without doubt we are getting bullied on the ball. Everybody knows what League Two football is

“We’ve got to look at areas of the pitch we need to be strong – and that’s ironically in both boxes, and then the flare in the wide areas”

“At the moment we haven’t got that so we are trying to address that and that’s what the owners are trying to do.

“We need to try and get through to Christmas and then see if we can maybe change the dynamics of the squad – but knowing full well what is required in this league.”

Following Blackwell’s thorough assessment of the squad, he was rest assured that the board will take on his advice and make the changes required to steer the club away from trouble.

He said: “I think they are well aware themselves of the situation. You’ve only got to watch the games to know that physically we’ve struggled against teams that are more physical than us.

“You bake a cake and the recipe has got to be right. It’s not all about height, it’s also about technical ability, speed, power.

“But every sport is power and pace. We haven’t got enough of that at this moment in time, but we’ve recognised that and are trying to correct it.”

Crawley have signed four free agent in the past fortnight. Now with a squad of 32, Blackwell has the challenge of sorting through the squad and picking his best 11.

He said: “First of all you look at attitude and you look at ability and you look at what they do in training everyday. Tthat’s a big for any coach what they do on the training ground, and that can influence your decision.

“I’ve seen these now for two weeks. I’ve seen them on the training ground, I’ve now seen them in the game and all my experience in the game tells me I know what they can do and what they can’t do.”

The Reds now have an extended break before their next game, having had this weekend’s game against Rotherham postponed.

When asked how he would tackle this next week, Blackwell said: “The great thing about football is everyday is different and problems arise out of nowhere sometimes, but the good thing for the next few weeks is that we’ve got no game in hand.

“We can now concentrate on the training ground. We are focussing on Fleetwood and how we are going to try and get a result against Fleetwood.”

#1966. Bradford City midfielder George Lapslie on perspective, family and silver lining with Michael Duff

In the difficult moments, there's a fair degree of empathy. Like earlier this year.

The Bradford City midfielder found himself out of the first-team squad during the 2025-26 run-in and his elder brother was also struggling for opportunities at National League South side Chelmsford City.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

While Lapslie junior had his own issues, he had perspective because his sibling has struggled significantly with injuries throughout his career.

Lapslie told The Yorkshire Post: "I'm in contact with my brother daily. He's now at Farnborough.

"My brother has struggled a lot in his career (with injuries) and it's probably a lot of the reason why I'm so grateful because he's struggled with multiple injuries.

"So if you compare it to what I've had, I've been able to play but I just can't play (not selected) on a matchday compared to not being able to play at all.

"I'm grateful for being able to stay fit and try and help the team when I do get a chance.

"When we speak, we try to keep it unrelated to football. But it came to a point where in March, it was like eight or nine squads in a row where you're not in. Then we're talking about what the future looked like.

"But apart from that, we try and keep it away from football because obviously we're both consumed with football all the time anyway."

The Bantams player has fought his way back into the first-team picture at City and is also hugely grateful for what he's got at a club which is in the Londoner's soul and his family's.

Family is everything to Lapslie and so are City.

His parents are regular visitors to Valley Parade, making the trip up from the south. His nan was also in attendance at the club's EFL Cup win at Leyton Orient earlier this autumn.

There were touching scenes after the game when Lapslie embraced her. His grandfather, who had been a big source of inspiration in his life and a huge supporter, had passed away a few weeks earlier.

The Waltham Forest born player's pride at stepping out in the claret and amber is not the sort that can be manufactured.

When told back in January that his opportunities could be restricted, he backed himself to earn another chance.

Late in the summer window, despite some interest from elsewhere, the 29-year-old did not push for a move.

Although he was brought up at the other end of the country, Bradford feels like home.

He continued: "My eldest is a Bradford fan. I was doing reading with her the other day and the man's name in the book was Brad and she was like: 'oh, Bradford, Bradford!'

"So everything is Bradford at the house. We've got Bradford flags, Bradford stickers. They've (kids) got their Bradford kits, obviously.

"I'm going to follow Bradford for the rest of my life. That's a fact and I'll be very surprised if my eldest doesn't as well.

"My parents probably come up twice a month to come see us. So we get together quite a bit."

Used pretty sparingly by former Bantams chief Graham Alexander last season and in the first part of the current one, Lapslie is doing his level best to impress the new 'gaffer,' Michael Duff.

Despite spending time on the periphery, Lapslie's relationship with Alexander remained a good one. But it was not lost upon him that a change of manager could work in his favour.

In all competitions, he has started four of City's last five matches. His goal in Saturday's FA Cup rout against Marine was his first in over a year.

Lapslie acknowledged: "When the gaffer (Alexander) left, some people did make comments to me and said: 'maybe I bet you're happy about it'.

"But I wasn't; I'd got on with Graham. But obviously, with a new gaffer coming in, there are more opportunities and I was excited about that. I'm grateful because this gaffer has given me a couple of opportunities.

"I think I've done okay and I think more opportunities will come. So, yes, I'm excited and still believe that I can make it really work here."

While Lapslie was left out of Duff's first match-day league squad for the home game against Stevenage on October 17, there was a silver lining.

After naming his side, Duff bumped into Lapslie with his young family at Valley Parade. What could have been an awkward moment turned into a positive conversation as the pair got to know each other and had an extended chat with his young family present.

Lapslie continued: "It speaks volumes about him as well, to take the time to get to know my daughters because he could have easily just moved on there and he didn't. He took the time to get to know us. So yes, I'm really grateful for that."

#1964. He had the world at his feet when he signed for Real Madrid at 13, mixing with Zidane and Ronaldo. Now Jack Harper plays in Italy's Serie D... but he's not giving up on his Scotland dream

Published: 13:06 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 17:10 EST, 6 November 2026

Whatever the Italian word is for ‘steamie’, the steady migration of Scottish players to Serie A has been the talk of it.

The exploits of Scott McTominay and Billy Gilmour at Napoli have been comprehensively documented. Che Adams is thriving at Torino where he now shares a dressing room with Nathan Patterson. You can count Kieron Bowie, Josh Doig, Lennon Miller and Liam Henderson among the diaspora, too.

However, another Scot’s switch to Italy has largely flown under the radar. Back in July, Jack Harper, the former Real Madrid wonderkid and presumed saviour of Scottish football, signed a one-year deal with ASD Nuova Igea Virtus.

Currently playing in Serie D, the fourth tier of the Italian national league pyramid, the Sicilian part-timers were founded in 1946 and subsequently re-founded in 1964, 2011 and again in 2019. Which is to say they’ve had a complicated existence.

Harper can surely relate. Now 30, the Malaga-born frontman was 13 when he first made headlines, signing with Real Madrid after impressing in a youth football tournament. He spent almost six years with Los Blancos, learning his trade in its exalted ‘La Fabrica’ academy under the watchful eye of top coaches, Fernando Morientes and Zinedine Zidane amongst them.

If he wasn’t bumping into Cristiano Ronaldo in the swimming pool, he was having a blether with Gareth Bale or studying Luka Modric. All the while, he was quietly developing, establishing himself as one of the top scorers in multiple age groups within the academy.

Jack Harper now plies his trade in Italy's Serie D with Sicilian club ASD Nuova Igea Virtus

Soon after his 18th birthday, and with Real’s youth structure under review, he decided to swap Madrid for Brighton, signing a two-year deal with the then English Championship side. He couldn’t have known it at the time, but Harper’s move to the Amex Stadium was the start of a frustratingly nomadic decade.

A catalogue of injuries and bad luck kick-started a footballing odyssey that has taken in spells at Malaga, Getafe, Alcorcón, Cartagena and Villarreal, as well as Racing Santander, Hércules, Marbella, Linense and, more recently, Spanish fourth-division outfit Linares.

Harper joined the latter ahead of the 2025-26 season and made an encouraging start, scoring four goals in his first nine appearances before, once again, injury struck. He spent almost four months on the sidelines and, when the campaign ended, he found himself a free agent once more.

‘At that point, I decided to forget all about it until after the World Cup,’ he tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘I said to my family I didn’t want to think about it. I needed to just disconnect.’

He and his brother Ryan travelled to Miami to take in Scotland’s final group match against Brazil and, standing shoulder to shoulder with the Tartan Army in the stands of the Hard Rock Stadium, he allowed himself to wonder what might have been.

‘It was definitely in the back of my mind that I could have been on the pitch because that’s the type of person I am,’ says Harper. ‘I know that if the road was a bit straighter and I’d had just a little more luck, then absolutely, I could have been there representing my country.

Harper had the world at his feet when he signed for Real Madrid at the tender age of 13

‘Years ago, I was knocking on the door when I was playing in Spain. I was called up to the 30-man squad several times but then the injuries started to hit and the door kind of closed. So yeah, of course I was at the stadium thinking I should have been playing. I know the level of football I’m capable of. I just never got a chance to show it.

‘But being there was a cool experience. The atmosphere was unbelievable and to see us taking on a Brazil side dressed in the yellow jerseys with those five stars on them, it was incredible. The World Cup’s the pinnacle of football. I was just glad to be part of it somehow.’

After that party in the US, Harper returned to Spain to discover he was a man in demand.

‘I had a few interesting offers on the table,’ he smiles. ‘I spoke with my partner and we agreed that, whilst our preference was to stay in Spain, it might be wise for us to consider all options. Last season was really hard and so we thought that maybe a change of scenery would do us all good.

‘Next thing I knew, I had an offer from a team in Iraq. There was an opportunity with a team in Thailand, too. That was very, very close to being done. But then an agent contacted me out of the blue with some deals from Italy. Soon enough, we were packing our bags and moving to Sicily.’

Despite the relative proximity of the two countries, Harper insists Spanish and Italian football could not be more different.

Harper rubbed shoulders with the game's leading lights in Spain, including Cristiano Ronaldo

Zinedine Zidane was just beginning his coaching career during Harper's time at the Bernabeu

‘It’s been a bit of a culture shock,’ he admits. ‘Football in Italy is much more physical. I don’t think I touched a ball for the first ten days of pre-season. It was all about getting fit and not worrying about the technical side of things.

‘It’s different, but that’s why I’m here. I needed to get out of my comfort zone. I feel like I’ve got it all to prove. Nobody really knows me here, I don’t know the language... it’s not easy.

‘But maybe that’s what I need. You know, thirty’s still young. I could have another decade-plus of playing in front of me. So, the plan is to get fit, stay fit and hopefully start climbing the leagues again. The hunger is still there.’

He adds: ‘I’ve kind of been on an opposite journey to a lot of people. I started at a huge club, maybe the biggest club in the world; I’ve had a good contract with a La Liga team; I’ve played in front of my hometown fans and heard them chanting my name. So, I know what it’s like to be there. It doesn’t scare me in the slightest. I’ve had a taste of it and I’m hungry for more.

‘Cristiano Ronaldo has shown how long it’s possible to stay at the top level. So, too, Karim Benzema. Even Harry Kane. What is he now, 33? And he’s just had the best year of his career, winning the Ballon d’Or. It’s not that long ago people were writing forwards off at that age. So, no, I’m still motivated and I don’t see any reason why, with a wee bit of luck, I can’t keep playing until I’m close to my forties.’

If Harper’s self-belief and resilience sound impressive, it’s because he’s had ample opportunity to work on them. In addition to his various injury issues, he’s had to contend with the weight of expectation that comes with being on the books of Real Madrid, intense scrutiny from a very young age, and, of course, plenty of rejection.

Harper moved to Brighton in 2015 but his career failed to take flight with the Seagulls

Perhaps the most memorable example of the latter came in 2015 when he was left out of the Scotland Under-19 squad by then-coach Ricky Sbragia. The former Sunderland boss triggered a backlash from former players, fans and pundits alike when he dismissed Harper as ‘a luxury player’ that his team couldn’t accommodate.

Spanish football journalist Graham Hunter described it as a ‘retrograde, almost prehistoric decision’. Harper’s dad, John, branded the description ‘harsh’, warning that Scotland could lose his son to the Spanish national team.

Sbragia subsequently apologised for his choice of words but Harper admits it took him some time to get over.

‘It was hard to deal with,’ he nods, ‘especially considering the love I have for Scotland. I might have been born in Spain, but I’ve got Scottish blood pumping through me. Honestly, the prospect of playing for Scotland was always more exciting to me than playing for Real Madrid. But that was just the mentality some people had at that time.

‘I was probably the most high-profile victim of that way of thinking but there would have been others as well, players who maybe weren’t as physical and so were written off. But I would definitely say times have changed. You can see that with more technical players like Billy Gilmour coming through and being successful.

‘The game has moved on from that kind of thinking and it’s a good thing, I think, for Scotland that it has.’

Harper, in action for Getafe, has played for a host of Spanish clubs and wanted a new challenge

Whilst his international experience amounts to a handful of age-grade caps, Harper has not yet given up on playing again for his country.

‘The beautiful thing about football is that things can change quickly, especially if you’re a striker. You only need a season or a season and a half of scoring goals, and your career can lift off again. There are so many examples of that, maybe now more than ever.

‘So, that’s the thing that keeps me motivated every day when I go to training. If I can get into a good rhythm, score goals and stay fit, then who knows what might happen? I still have that dream and that hunger to play for Scotland. That might seem a bit crazy to some people. Honestly, sometimes it even seems a bit crazy to me. But it’s the thing that drives me and it’ll continue to drive me either until it happens or I retire.’

Harper admits he would love to experience playing in Scotland before he hangs up his boots, having come close to doing so on multiple occasions in the past.

‘I’ve had phone calls where it’s been like, “Okay, it’s going to get done” and then, for one reason or another, it hasn’t happened,’ he says. ‘I came pretty close to joining St Johnstone one time, and Falkirk as well many years ago. The last couple of years, there’s been interest from some Championship sides. It’s a challenge I’m definitely up for and something I’d like to make happen.’

#1962. Savio scores on debut as Spurs cruise past Charlton in Carabao Cup

It looked like this was going to be a night for “one of their own”, but Tottenham Hotspur’s latest big-money arrival, Sávio, stole the headlines to crank up the excitement at his new club.

Mikey Moore had set Spurs on their way to what proved a comfortable Carabao Cup success over Championship club Charlton Athletic and heard his name sung by the home fans.

But Sávio stepped off the substitutes’ bench to take the limelight with a late goal just a few days after completing his expensive switch from Manchester City, and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is demanding many more to come.

“A perfect day for him,” said De Zerbi. “His biggest improvement is to increase the number of goals. He is one of the best wingers, but the best wingers score many goals and I spoke with him two days ago, and we put the goal at 10-12 goals.

“We need 10-12 goals from the wingers. Last season, we suffered too much because the number of goals were not enough.”

"What an introduction!"Sávio scores a brilliant goal on his Spurs debut! 👏 pic.twitter.com/WgmcfgeNpX

Having watched some of Tottenham’s signings fall to a 3-0 Premier League defeat by Brentford a few days earlier, Sávio’s late impact was the perfect lift for the Spurs supporters.

The club have committed to spending almost £400m this summer, leading to debate by outsiders over whether it will prove to be money well spent and huge waves of excitement within the fanbase.

A deal that could be worth as much as £85m, if add-ons are achieved, for Sávio certainly raised some eyebrows, but the Brazilian provided the perfect response by scoring just 11 minutes into his debut as a late substitute.

In the 82nd minute, Sávio cut in from the flank and scored with a shot past Charlton goalkeeper Tiernan Brooks. He and the Spurs crowd thought he had a second a few minutes later, but his shot hit Ben Davies on its way into the net and the defender was credited with the goal.

Having sung for Moore earlier in the game, the Spurs fans wasted no time in trying out their new song for Sávio, inspired by the Spandau Ballet hit Gold.

Moore has been expected to move to Cologne on loan, but provided a reminder of his talent by opening the scoring in the first half with only his second goal for the club.

What a hit from Mikey Moore! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/OgSM4qhiqs

“We have to understand the best solution,” De Zerbi said. “I would like to keep him. He’s young but a good player, but we can’t make the wrong decision. He needs to play, he needs to get games inside him.”

Cutting in from the right, where Sávio is primed to play, Moore surged past his marker and shot from just inside the box. Brooks should have stopped it, but the ball flew past him and into the net.

Three minutes after Moore’s opener, Dominic Solanke scored his first goal since March to offer a reminder of what he can still give De Zerbi, who is poised to welcome Omar Marmoush to Tottenham.

Buoyed by his first-half goal, Moore skipped his way around a couple of tackles at the start of the second period but his low cross was cut out. The Spurs fans responded by singing “he’s one of our own.”

Substitute Kevin Danso netted with his first touch from a header, before Sávio was introduced to steal the show, despite a late consolation goal from Charlton’s Lloyd Jones.

Kevin Danso scores with his first touch since coming on! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/oqUU7wjoJW

The victory set up a tough third-round trip to Anfield to face Liverpool for Tottenham, but De Zerbi said: “It’s a great game. If we want to win the competition we have to win the games.

“Sometimes in this competition, it can happen that you play against big teams. It’s a great challenge for the players, for me, for our clubs. We have to arrive ready to play in our style, with personality, ready to play a game following the work we are doing on the training ground.”

It is all over in north London and Tottenham have booked their place in the third round of the League Cup with a comfortable 5-1 win over Charlton.

Newcastle have just about got past West Brom, winning 3-2 in the end, and they book their place in the third round.

Savio thinks he has his second in quick succession but it will go down as Davies’ goal. Savio’s shot was on target but it deflects off Davies and goes in for Tottenham’s fifth on the night.

Change for Tottenham as Williams-Barnett replaces Tel.

Savio is on for his Tottenham debut and replaces Solanke. Savio only joined Tottenham yesterday but makes his first appearance for the club tonight.

Kevin Danso scores with his first touch since coming on! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/oqUU7wjoJW

Roberto De Zerbi is turning to his bench and making a triple change as Van de Ven, Danso and Porro come on.

The first half in north London is brought to an end and Tottenham take a 2-0 lead into the break thanks to goals from Moore and Solanke. Tottenham looked rather lethargic for a lot of that first half but two goals in quick succession has Roberto De Zerbi’s side in control. As the players head off, the DJ pays homage to the late Dolly Parton by blasting out Nine to Five.

Roberto De Zerbi is quickly out of his seat!

A place in the League Cup third round is at stake as Tottenham host Charlton in a London derby at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. The last competitive meeting between these sides came in the FA Cup back in January 2011, with Tottenham winning that game 3-0 at White Hart Lane. A then 19-year-old Andros Townsend made his debut that day and scored, with Jermain Defoe scoring a brace.

Tottenham’s Premier League campaign got off to the worst possible start as they lost 3-0 at Brentford last weekend. Tottenham have been very busy during this summer transfer window and that has continued this week. Savio (formerly Savinho) has arrived from Manchester City in a deal that could be worth £85m and the Brazilian could make his Tottenham debut tonight, having been registered in time.

“I think in attacking positions we need players capable one-on one, to create something, to create a chance to score,” Roberto De Zerbi said. “In terms of one-on-one, he [Savio] is one of the best players, especially since 2024. He can play on the right side, on the left side. I have known him from a long time, I spoke with him when he went to Manchester City. He is a big player for us.

“I do not know if I am the right man [to get the most out of Savio], but for sure he has to achieve. I think a player who is so good in one-on-one, so good at creating chances to score, to be complete, he has to score. If you analyse the other best wingers in the world, many of them, they score 10 to 15 goals per season. He has the qualities. Maybe his habits, he has to change habits, because he has to be focused on the assists, the one-on-one dribbling and also to score.”

Omar Marmoush is closing in on an initial loan deal from Manchester City but that move is not complete and thus he is not available for Tottenham tonight. Micky van der Ven and Pedro Porro are both available having missed Tottenham’s loss at Brentford but the hosts are still without Xavi Simons, Pape Sarr, Dejan Kulusevski and Wilson Odobert.

Charlton have made the perfect start to their Championship campaign; a 2-1 home win over Derby was followed up by a 2-1 victory at recently-relegated West Ham. Nathan Jones’ side earned their place in the League Cup second round with a 3-1 win at Cheltenham in the first round.

“We have to be very organised and very professional, they [Tottenham] are a top team,” Jones said. “They have a great manager and a brilliant group of players. They already had a Premier League squad and they have spent, what is reaching about, I do not know, £300 million or something like that. It is a wonderful test, we have to be right near our best and do both sides of the game very well. Of course, you want to test yourself against the best managers and you want to test yourself against the best teams. For us, this is not our priority, the Championship is our priority, but this is the next game and therefore it is the most important.”

#1960. Home wobbles are a puzzle for Horsham FC boss after AFC Totton defeat

The Hornets saw their five-match unbeaten run in National League South come to an end at home to the Stags, Saturday’s game finishing 3-2 to the visitors.

Horsham have won just twice at home in the league in 2026-27, recording eight points in as many games.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

That is in stark contrast to the Hornets’ away form. They have taken 14 points from eight games and have yet to be beaten on the road.

And their home performances in the league have confounded Di Paola.

He told us: “It’s annoying. There’s been a few at home where you’re scratching your head as to why you’ve not got anything out of them.

“Maidstone we should have got more out of, Farnham we should have got more out of, Totton we should have got more out of. There’s been lots of opportunities for us to do better at home – and we have to do better at home.

“It’s hard to put your finger on why because we’re quite dominant in these games. I hate stats but we had 60 per cent possession on Saturday, double the amount of shots, double everything really – but it doesn’t mean anything.

“At home there seems to be a common thread where we dominate games but don’t capitalise – yet when we go away we’re perhaps not as dominant but we pick up points.

“Maybe we need to have a reset in how we approach home games because it’s clearly not working.

“But if you look at every metric apart from points and wins, we’re doing really well so there’s something fundamentally wrong.”

Totton led twice in the first half only for the Hornets to strike back both times through Charlie Hester-Cook and Ryan Bartley.

Josh Sims hit what proved to be the Stags’ winner on 72 minutes to bring Horsham’s unbeaten streak to an end.

Defeat to Totton saw the Hornets drop two places to 12th.

Di Paola added: “They had three shots on target and scored all three. We just don’t capitalise when we’re on top. We don’t seem to be able to pull away from teams.

“We got back to 1-1 and then we gave away a really poor goal from a corner. We got it back to 2-2 and we’re on the march, but they’ve gone down the other end and scored and it’s almost game over.

“We were chasing it but they were able to park the bus and they just sat in and made it really hard for us to score – like we’ve done to teams.

“On Saturday – and you sound like an idiot – we did okay but we’ve given away a couple of sloppy goals. And I think you can give away sloppy goals due to the nature of the opposition.

“It was really frustrating off the back of a good spell of results. But that is going to happen. We’ve got to understand that this league is not easy. We’ve just got to reset and pick up a few wins.”

Horsham entertain National League South rivals Torquay United in the second round of the FA Trophy this Saturday.

#1958. Bayern Munich's £400,000-a-week 'risk' on Harry Kane: Dietmar Hamann reveals doubts about Ballon d'Or winner - and claims no English team would have matched mega contract offer

Published: 17:12 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 17:12 EST, 6 November 2026

Bayern Munich are taking a major 'risk' giving Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane a bumper new deal, according to former midfielder Didi Hamann.

Kane, 33, and Bayern Munich have agreed on a two-year contract extension worth £400,000 per week which will make him the world's highest-paid English sportsman.

But ex-Liverpool and Bayern man Hamann has suggested that this may prove to be a poor move given Kane's age and possible decline.

'Whether he'll still be scoring goals in the coming years, we'll see. He's 33 years old and will be 36 when the contract expires. There's obviously a certain risk involved,' Champions League winner Hamann told Sky Germany.

Hamann then went on to justify his bizarre comments by saying: 'He didn't play well for England at the European Championship two years ago, and he had problems in the last two knockout matches at the World Cup.'

The ex-Germany international also suggested that staying at Bayern was the best deal Kane was going to get at this stage in his career, saying: 'I don't think there were any major suitors from England.

Harry Kane has signed a two-year-long contract extension with Bayern but Didi Hamann is not convinced this is the right move for the Bavarians

Speaking with Sky Germany Dietmar Hamann expressed concerns over his old side offering Kane such a large deal

'They would have taken him for 20 or 30 million, but Bayern would probably have wanted at least half or three-quarters back this summer of the 100 million euros they had to pay Tottenham for Kane in 2023.

'I don't think anyone would have paid that. That's why the contract extension is something they probably couldn't have done any differently.'

Hamann is arguably taking a harsh view on Kane's new deal considering how the Englishman has performed since arriving in Germany.

In three seasons at the Allianz he has 102 Bundesliga goals in as many games as well as 28 assists, winning the Bundesliga Golden Boot every year since his arrival.

The Englishman's goals have fired Bayern to two back-to-back Bundesliga titles and a DFB-Pokal triumph.

But clearly all of this is not enough for Hamann who has previously critiqued Kane's performances in Germany saying that last season his role in Kompany's Bayern side was 'unacceptable.'

In his Sky Germany column the former defensive midfielder wrote: 'I don't know if Kompany is happy that Harry Kane is no longer playing exclusively as a striker.

'It's not acceptable to me that Kane is winning balls in his own penalty area, because that's not his job at all.'

#1952. Martin O'Neill relaxed over Kasper Hogh scoring drought as Celtic boss hails Dane's display against Besiktas

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:30 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 17:30 EST, 6 November 2026

Martin O'Neill is adamant that he’s not overly concerned about Kasper Hogh’s goal drought — despite the Dane failing to find the net in 15 matches.

Celtic’s record signing at £11million from Bodo/Glimt, the forward looked set to be a huge hit when he scored a hat-trick at Kilmarnock on August 9 only to go off the boil.

His hopes of ending a barren run against Besiktas on Thursday ended when he was taken off 13 minutes from time, with substitutes Callum Osmand and Camilo Duran climbing off the bench to seal a dramatic 3-2 for O’Neill’s men.

But while O’Neill shared Hogh’s frustration at not getting among the goals again, he made a point of telling him that he should have been proud of his other work on the night.

‘I did, absolutely,’ he explained. ‘I want centre-forwards to be able to hold it and that is what he did.

‘He is not Duran, he is not a dribbler. But if he can do this for us against strong opposition it will stand him in good stead.’

O'Neill admits his record-signing is currently struggling for confidence in front of goal

Hogh hasn't found the net since firing a hat-trick in a 5-1 win over Kilmarnock on August 9

With his player not in the latest Denmark squad, O’Neill believes confidence may be an issue. But he stressed: ‘I think Thursday night will be good for him. I said to him that I’m not worried about whether he scores a goal.

‘Of course, you want centre-forwards to score and, of course, centre-forwards live on them. But I said to him that last night I wanted him to be strong and fight when the ball is played up to him.

'I thought in terms of holding the ball up and bringing people into the game, that he did really well.’

Duran stole the headlines against the Turks, though, with his double securing Celtic’s first win in the Europa League and bringing his personal tally for the season to 13.

‘At this minute, he is on fire,’ O’Neill said of the Colombian. ‘He can play wide right, he has done that. He has played wide left for his other club. But centre forward is where he is dynamic.’

Asked if it was increasingly difficult to start Hogh ahead of Duran through the middle, O’Neill said: ‘We will see. We made five changes on Thursday night because it was necessary.

‘Centre-forwards need a goal but that performance there against European opposition will give him confidence.

‘I don’t know what side we will play on Sunday. But this lad has scored goals in the Champions League remember.

'He will get a confidence boost from Thursday night in terms of doing that part of the game well. But it will be nice for him to score a goal.’

While O’Neill’s side now focus on Kilmarnock, the win over Besiktas has breathed new life into their European campaign. With three points on the board at the midway point, two further wins from their matches with Torreense, Omonia, Marseille and Union Saint-Gilloise may see them qualify for the knockout round.

‘It was really pleasing and really important,’ O’Neill said of Thursday’s dramatic victory. ‘We conceded some ground in the game which was to be expected, but I thought defensively we were really, really strong.

‘From the European side, we have given ourselves a chance. We will have to go and win away from home and it will not be easy. We are looking forward to Sunday and we will look to take it on.’

#1951. 'I can't lie' - Leeds United winger Daniel James lifts lid on frustration of not playing

Leeds United winger Daniel James has conceded there is frustration that comes with a lack of playing time.

The jet-heeled wideman is rated highly by Whites boss Daniel Farke and has been a key figure throughout the German’s reign.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

However, he has found opportunities limited this season and managed just one start in the Premier League.

James, now away on international duty with Wales, has discussed the importance of being a team player in an interview with the official Leeds website.

The 29-year-old said: “I think we've had a great start. I think it was very important for us to get a result coming to this international break. I thought we were really good, put on a great performance.

“But yeah, as a player, obviously, I can't lie, obviously you do get frustrated not playing, but you have to give your all for the team, because ultimately it's a team game and, even if you're not getting as many minutes as you want, you want to perform and train every day, push players that are starting as well.

“I played against Bournemouth, a couple of weeks ago. I felt really good, but ultimately it's always down to the manager of what team he wants to set up in. But I've just got to be ready every time, and I feel like I am.

“I've got myself in a good place to whenever I'm called upon, that I feel ready. And I feel really good coming to this camp.”

James will turn 30 next year and has the additional responisibilites that come with being a senior player. Not only does he have plenty of experience, the former Swansea City star is Leeds’ longest-serving player having joined from Manchester United back in 2021.

He said: “I'm definitely just as quick. I think obviously I've had a few injuries and sometimes it's taken me a little bit longer [to recover], but I think, as I become more of a senior player, it's about how much you can maintain that, because I think it's not just about being quick once. You want to be able to do that the whole game.

"And I think as I've become more senior, I've learned to work around that a lot more. But it's something that I work on every day because, ultimately, I want to play, I want my career to be as long as possible. But I want to be as quick as long as possible.

“I think when you start getting 30 plus, I think it's about how much you can maintain it. But it's something that I'm always working on, and will do for the rest of my career.”
