#1920. Man United fans urge supporters to REFUSE to buy booze at Old Trafford as groups ramp up anti-Glazer and Sir Jim Ratcliffe protests ahead of Sunday's clash with Aston Villa

Published: 04:44 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 04:49 EST, 7 November 2026

Manchester United fan groups are calling for a booze boycott at Sunday’s game against Aston Villa at Old Trafford as part of their protests against the club’s owners.

Supporters have revived the green and gold campaign against the Glazer family in recent weeks, with minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe also in their sights.

During Tuesday’s Champions League win over Roma at Old Trafford, green and gold balloons were released from the Stretford End before kick-off and tennis balls were thrown onto the pitch in the 20th minute.

Now groups including Reclaim the Stretford End, The 1958, The Red Army, Manchester United Youth Supporters’ Club, South Stand United and Retro Reds are urging fans to hit the owners in the pocket by refusing to buy alcohol in the stadium at the Villa game.

Supporters have been asked to release balloons again when the teams come out before the match, but to respect the minute’s silence on Remembrance Sunday.

The joint organisers say they are protesting against the ownership, the plans to knock down Old Trafford and build a new 100,000-seater stadium next door, United’s debts of more than £1billion, and what they say is a decline in standards throughout the club and the disrespect being shown to match-going fans.

Manchester United supporter groups have urged fans to follow an alcohol boycott

Fan groups are ramping up protests against the Glazer family and co-owners INEOS

Details of the new protest have emerged after it was confirmed that three people were arrested for throwing tennis balls onto the pitch during the Roma game. The game had to be halted temporarily as the players helped to remove them.

Greater Manchester Police made a further eight arrests including four for assault, two for public order offences, one for fraud and one for possession of Class B drugs.

But the game passed off without the serious trouble that has marred previous meetings between United and Roma dating back to their first meeting in the quarter-final of the Champions League in April 2007 when Italian riot police were widely criticised for wading into English fans after they reacted to being pelted with missiles by Roma supporters.

United famously won the return leg 7-1 when police made 18 arrests after fans clashed outside Old Trafford.

#1918. Sheffield Wednesday 0 Accrington Stanley 4: Young Owls unable to make the case in front of Dave Challinor

In what was effectively the second of two pre-season games for Dave Challinor before his league debut at home to Plymouth Argyle on Saturday, there was no real rush to put names forward.

If a Sunday evening FA Cup first-round defeat at Oldham Athletic was fairly humdrum, a Football League Trophy game watched by 5,472 hardy souls on a cold night (decide for yourself if the prefix "fool" is needed) was much more low-key, with both sides already guaranteed a place in the last 32 of this horribly bloated competition.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Between them, Wednesday's starting XI had a combined 89 league starts for the club, 75 of them belonging to captain Sean Fusire, Gabriel Otegbayo and Jarvis Thornton, none at all to Connal Trueman, Joel Akpobi and Samuel Duruh, nor Denny Oliver on his first start in any competition, or Louis Poland on his first appearance full stop.

Striker George Brown was making his first outing of an injury-hit 2026.

So there was not a great deal to take from Challinor's first Hillsborough match as Owls manager, except perhaps the fact that he lined his team up in a 3-4-3, similar to what he did at Boundary Park before changing shape in the second half there.

Nor did anyone not already in his plans make a strong case to face the Pilgrims.

Needing a point to guarantee top spot and a home draw in the last 32, the young Owls were outclassed by League Two Accrington, who claimed it instead with a 4-0 win.

Oliver put a free-kick onto the roof of the net, but otherwise the early chances fell to the visitors.

Seamus Conneely missed the target in the 18th, as did Ronan Darcy when he caught a volley sweetly quickly after.

Nigerian-born right winger Duruh, who learnt his football in Spain and has also had a loan spell with Beverley Town, beat his man in the 21st minute but his cross was cut out, albeit unconvincingly. He was the pick of the youngsters.

Two minutes later Fusire ought to have buried Akpobi's ball in from a couple of yards out, and was lucky the linesman had flagged for an earlier offence.

But that was pretty much that for Wednesday's first-half threat, barring the shot Brown made space for right at the end of it, but could not force through the defenders in front of him.

Trueman was busy in the final 15 minutes of the half, even if Alex Henderson's shot was straight at him. His next effort six minutes later forced a decent low save with strong hands.

Trueman did even better to deny Shaun Whaley in the 38th minute when the centre-forward really should have converted Henderson's ball in, but the goalkeeper got across his box well.

It was a temporary reprieve, though, Accrington taking the lead a minute later when the Owls failed to get the ball clear after Farrend Rawson struck their crossbar. Josh Smith eventually forced the ball in.

Three minutes later the lead was doubled, the ball coming in from the right to Charlie Brown to find the net from 20 yards. Good grief.

It was Brown who put a free-kick wide early in the second half before Duruh, now on the left, forced a save with a chance made by his own dribble.

It would have been three on the hour but for a big Otegbayo block on Tyler Walton, and should have been again when Darcy put an excellent chance wide.

Seven substitutes at once – three for the Owls – had added to the pre-season feel by then.

One of the later changes, Kleven de Oliveira forced a good save in the 79th minute, with Thornton doing likewise from the follow-up.

Accrington wrapped things up in the 86th minute when Wednesday were caught out trying to press the ball in midfield and it was worked down the inside-left channel for Charlie Warren to finish calmly.

Charlie Caton put the tin lid on it with a fourth goal in the fifth of seven added minutes.

It had been a forgettable night for the home side, but Saturday is when things start for real for Challinor.

Sheffield Wednesday: Trueman; Otegbayo, Weaver, McGhee (Hatfield 62); Fusire, Oliver, Thornton, Poland (de Oliveira 74); Duruh (Onoh 62), Brown (Kay HT), Akpobi (Liddell 62).

Accrington Stanley: Rogerson; Moore, Rawson (Matthews 62), J Smith; Walton (Caton 62), Conneely (Grant 62), O Smith, Brown; Darcy, Henderson (Mols 62); Whalley.

Unused substitutes: Moulden, Anderson, Warren.

#1916. Iraola fumes at bungling fourth official for costing Liverpool a penalty

Andoni Iraola wanted to talk about his team and their need to improve but how could he concentrate on something so straightforward when he had seen something so bizarre?

It is important, first and foremost, to explain this is not painting a narrative about Liverpool being unfortunate. Far from it. Iraola hissed his dismay that Nottingham Forest had shown more intensity and been the better team for long periods in an entertaining 2-2 draw.

But the penalty that changed the contest? Iraola, his coaching staff, even the supporters behind the dugout had been left flabbergasted that the malfunctioning number board of fourth official Tim Robinson presented an avenue for Forest to exploit.

Iraola had tried to make a triple change, wanting to introduce Ryan Gravenberch, Kostas Tsimikas and Rio Ngumoha, but as Robinson pressed buttons to no avail and everyone in Red became frustrated, Forest substitute Liam Delap took a quick throw and the Liverpool house almost caved in.

Neco Williams, once of Liverpool, surged into the penalty area, Alisson Becker arrived a fraction too late after the defender got his shot away and took his old team-mate down. Morgan Gibbs-White exacerbated the damage when sending Alisson the wrong way and this was the last thing a manager wanting to make an impression on a big day needed to see but this was reality.

Alisson takes out Neco Williams and Forest have a penalty! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fX2flY3Tob

Gibbs-White converts from the spot to restore Forest's lead! 🌳🎯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/jeoPiXPArw

“I cannot explain because I don’t have an explanation,” Iraola said. “I wanted to make those substitutions about three minutes before. I mean, it was two, three, four times the ball had gone out. I still don’t know the reason why we couldn’t make the subs.

“I think [the fourth official] was having some problems with the board or something. It [the penalty] wouldn’t have happened if I had made the sub. I asked. I had complained the previous time. The supporters were shouting and they were aware of the situation. But I don’t know what happened and I don’t know why they have given the penalty.”

"A professional fourth official cannot take three minutes." 😳Andoni Iraola was not happy with the time taken to get the substitutes' board ready.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fMfYOjQJPd

He did know, though, why Liverpool had needed to drag themselves off the deck again for the second week in a row. Iraola has shown in his opening weeks on Merseyside that he is not someone who seeks excuses.

“A lack of intensity hurt us,” Iraola said with obvious disdain and it was only down to a show of character in the second period that a slovenly first half did not enable Forest to win at Anfield for the third consecutive year, for all that the travelling fans thought it was “happening again!”

Forest, bruised after two defeats in four days to Leeds, looked like an Oliver Glasner side. They were aggressive and well organised, the only failing was that physically they could not see the job through, but the Austrian insisted that will change in due course.

Once Glasner is settled in and he gets his transfer business done – “definitely one, possibly two and probably three,” was his mischievous reply to how the window will unfold – Forest will be a formidable proposition, especially if the first 45 minutes are a barometer.

They had been knocking on the door before Dan Ndoye eventually broke the deadlock, sweeping a left-footed drive past Alisson after Igor Jesus had won a header from a long clearance. It was a simple goal, marginally onside, but it was absolutely deserved.

Ndoye gives Forest the lead at Anfield! 🌳🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ag0oZ7UjTm

“There were many positive aspects,” said Glasner. “It has been a three-game week; some players played. We are getting more and more fitness, that is just the foundation of how we want to play. It is just a point but it still feels a bit frustrating, so we have to stay humble.”

"I think we were very poor in the first half." 😤Andoni Iraola gives his assessment of Liverpool's performance against Nottingham Forest.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/COZfhwkLeX

Neco Williams and James McAtee react to Nottingham Forest's draw at Anfield 🌳🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BjX0p1yQ1m

The playmaker added another goal and assist to his tally this afternoon.

20 - Morgan Gibbs-White has been directly involved in 20 goals in 2026 (15 goals, 5 assists), the joint-most of any Premier League player in all competitions (level with Haaland).His 13 goals in the Premier League in 2026 are also the most of any player.Decisive. pic.twitter.com/p1wQFwXvsI

Liverpool and Forest are both made to wait for their first Premier League wins of the season as the two sides play out a pulsating 2-2 draw at Anfield.

Full-time scenes at Anfield as Liverpool and Nottingham Forest share the points 🤝📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/WqOpfU38es

Sels calmly comes out to claim a deep cross to relieve the pressure on Forest. Munoz runs back to dispossess Delap and win a free kick, giving Liverpool another chance to launch the ball forward.

Glasner makes a very late double change as Hudson-Odoi and Dominguez replace McAtee and Igor Jesus.

There will be five minutes of added time. Liverpool continue their relentless search for a third goal, while Forest are holding on.

It’s wave after wave of Liverpool pressure. Forest are camped inside their own half. Igor Jesus and Delap are chasing every loose ball, but Forest are struggling to get out at the moment.

Munoz’s goal has provided another twist in this pulsating encounter. Isak wins a free kick in such dangerous territory and Szoboszlai steps up to take it. The Hungarian slams a venomous effort wide of the far post. Can either side find a late winner?

What an incredible finish! Wirtz threads a delightful pass through to Munoz. With his back to goal, the winger swivels and takes the ball on the outside of Murillo, before smashing a thunderous effort into the roof of the net, which brushes the crossbar on its way in.

Munoz, take a bow! 🤯👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/GD8IAdy2rJ

Igor Jesus does brilliantly to escape Nyoni, before he is pulled to the ground by Arajou, who is booked. It’s been an excellent defensive effort from Forest.

Iraola makes his final two alterations as Araujo and Nyoni replace Jacquet and Mac Allister.  Szoboszlai then swings such an inviting delivery into the penalty area, but Isak miscues his strike with his left foot.

Amid the chaos, Alisson was booked just before the penalty after appealing the decision and Iraola has ordered a triple change, taking off Kerkez, Frimpong and Gakpo for Tsimikas, Gravenberch and Ngumoha. This has seen Szoboszlai move out to right back.

Andoni Iraola is about to make his substitution and this is interesting because he had planned to introduce Rio Ngumoha, Kostas Tsimikas and Ryan Gravenberch 10 minutes ago but told them to sit down after Liverpool had equalised. Forest have put Liam Delap on, giving him his debut after completing his £45m move to the club.

The Forest captain sends Alisson the wrong way, powering a clinical penalty into the net. Gibbs-White demonstrates fantastic composure and Liverpool have it all to do again.

Gibbs-White converts from the spot to restore Forest's lead! 🌳🎯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/jeoPiXPArw

Delap showcases excellent initiative and takes a quick throw-in to send Williams through on goal. Alisson rushes out and catches Williams as he attempts to lob the goalkeeper. Williams crashes to the ground and the referee points to the spot. Alisson is furious. What a chance for Forest to restore their lead.

Alisson takes out Neco Williams and Forest have a penalty! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fX2flY3Tob

This game is being played at a ferocious pace and Forest’s club-record signing Delap enters the action as he replaces Ndoye. Can the former Chelsea striker mark his debut with a much-needed goal?

That leveller has injected so much energy into Liverpool. Anfield believes again. Isak really needed that goal.

So much credit must go to Gakpo. The winger shrugs off Williams and fires a pinpoint cross towards the back post. Isak is there and converts from close range. We’re set up for such an intriguing finale. Liverpool have the momentum now.

Isak equalises for Liverpool at the Kop end! 🔴🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/qKFxq2AqaB

Wirtz’s frustrating afternoon is compounded as he picks up a booking after hauling Murillo to the ground. Iraola looks to be readying some substitutions.

There is a very strange feeling here: it’s almost a case of the home fans waiting for Nottingham Forest to score a second goal rather than anticipating that Liverpool will equalise. The early buzz in the atmosphere has gone and that is because the gaps everyone can see in the make up of the team remain. How Bradley Barcola will transform this situation?

Jacquet’s pass is intercepted and Ndoye is released on the counter. He’s guided out wide by Van Dijk but still squeezes in a brilliant cross. Gibbs-White was running up the pitch in support and slowed down, meaning no one was there to turn in Ndoye’s delivery.

Munoz is the next player to be booked after reacting angrily to a decision. Iraola has to consider making some changes soon.

Aina catches Munoz with a late challenge and he’s the second Forest player to go into the referee’s book.

You can already see in this second half that there is acres of space for Forest to exploit on the counter as Liverpool push for a leveller. Munoz then heads a point-blank header over the bar. Luckily for the Spaniard, the offside flag was up against Gakpo.

We are back for the second half here at Anfield. Can Liverpool find a route back into this game or can Forest hold onto the three points?

It’s a bizarre situation for Liverpool. They could easily be level or be 2-0 down. But they trial just 1-0 at half-time. Wirtz and Gakpo are looking lively, but Isak has struggled to influence the game.

Dan Ndoye scores his first goal in the Premier League in 377 days 🤯 pic.twitter.com/tjSiGoSPyW

Forest have a slender one-goal advantage at the break after a frantic first half at Anfield. Ndoye curled the visitors into a well-deserved lead after 24 minutes, before Wirtz had a goal ruled out for offside. The German was then sensationally denied by Sels’ diving save as he tipped Wirtz’s header over the bar. Alisson then replicated Sels’ heroics, parrying Igor Jesus’ strike against the woodwork to stop Forest from doubling their lead.

What a move and what a save! Murillo sprays an inch-perfect pass out to Aina, who chops inside of Munoz and fires a low cross into Igor Jesus. The Forest striker shoots first-time from inside the penalty area, but his effort is sensationally parried onto the bar by Alisson. That is a world-class stop from the Brazilian goalkeeper.

A world-class save from Alisson denies Forest a second! 🤯🧤📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4NtzROILrU

Igor Jesus receives the game’s first yellow card after clipping Mac Allister with an unnecessary challenge.

Liverpool then fly forward again as Gakpo nutmegs Williams. His cross trickles through to Munoz at the back post. The ball is slightly behind Munoz and he leans back before shooting, causing his strike to narrowly sail over the bar.

There will be three minutes of added time to conclude this first half.

Liverpool are applying all the pressure at the end of this first half. At times, Forest have had every outfield player behind the ball.

Sels makes a superb save! Gakpo takes on his marker on the outside and fires in a cross which Wirtz meets. The attacker gets in between Schlager and Aina to win the header, but his effort is excellently tipped over the bar by Sels.

Out of nothing, Liverpool are level. McAtee attempts to play out from a deep position and his pass is intercepted by Wirtz. The ball breaks to Frimpong, who slips a clever pass to Wirtz. The German playmaker swivels and slides a low effort into the bottom corner. It’s a brilliant finish, but Frimpong was in an offside position before he provided the assist. VAR confirms this and Liverpool’s joy has been cut short. That is a huge let off for Forest, who need to be more careful with possession in deeper areas.

Following that Forest goal, there was a small flurry of Liverpool pressure, with Szoboszlai having a free kick punched away by Sels. Murillo is then very careless with the ball and is dispossessed. This allowed Mac Allister to play in Isak, but the striker is crowded out by multiple Forest defenders before he can get a shot away.

For the third season in a row, Nottingham Forest lead at Anfield. The goal had been coming, too. Liverpool were bright early but suddenly big gaps have started appearing and Forest are wily enough to exploit. There are lots of gripes around the stands about it being “too easy” and this knowledgeable crowd are right. A long ball forward and a simple flick has caused mayhem.

Forest are ahead and are well worth their lead. Sels launches a long ball up to Igor Jesus, who takes it down with an exquisite touch. The ball then breaks to Gibbs-White. The Forest captain plays in Ndoye and the winger curls a clinical effort into the far bottom corner to send the away support wild.

Ndoye gives Forest the lead at Anfield! 🌳🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ag0oZ7UjTm

Liverpool are struggling to find any space in and around Forest’s midfield and defence. Isak and Wirtz have been on the periphery as the time ticks over midway point of the first half.

Huge chance for Forest! McAtee drops deep and picks out Ndoye with a teasing cross. The forward meets the delivery and his header bounces wide. Upon the replays, there looks to have been a push on Frimpong by Ndoye. The referee’s whistle wasn’t sounded so it would have been interesting to see what would of happened if that chance had been converted.

It’s been a really frantic start to this game. Out of possession, Forest are retreating into a really rigid back five formation. Going forward, Aina and Williams are getting up the pitch at every opportunity.

Aina stands up an inviting cross to the back post for Ndoye, who heads it back into the danger zone. Igor Jesus latches onto it, but Jacquet makes a goal-saving tackle to block the striker’s close-range effort.

Sensational block from Jeremy Jacquet to deny Igor Jesus! 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/XuhO1GuE9F

Van Dijk clips a long ball over to the onrushing Isak as Liverpool look to burst forward on the counter. Isak races onto it and enters the penalty area, but he’s chased by Jair Cunha who matches the striker for pace. There’s a shoulder-to-shoulder, and the Forest defender bumps Isak off the ball, before Milenkovic comes back to mop up the danger.

Ndoye attempts to sprint in behind Liverpool’s defence. He’s chased by Jacquet and Ndoye can’t quite take the ball under his spell. That is an early warning sign for Liverpool.

The hosts then go up the other end as Mac Allister threads a delightful pass through to Gakpo. The Liverpool forward tries to swivel and shoot, but Williams tracks back and makes a crucial tackle.

Frimpong gets in behind Forest’s backline and attempts to pick out Gakpo with a cross aimed towards the back post. However, the ball bobbles and the Liverpool right back overhits his delivery.

A very intriguing team selected by Andoni Iraola and one that illustrates his confidence. It could be viewed as big call to drop Ryan Gravenberch and Rio Ngumoha but Victor Munoz and Alexis Mac Allister both made a difference when they were introduced at St James’s Park last Sunday and they warrant their inclusion. Munoz won’t be fit enough to play 90 minutes but it will be fascinating to watch him, particularly as Bradley Barcola will soon arrive to play in the same position on the left flank.

We are now under way at Anfield. Can Iraola mark his first competitive home game with a win or will Glasner get up and running with Forest?

A roaring rendition of You’ll Never Walk Alone has just boomed around Anfield. We will now observe a minute’s applause for Liverpool legend Kevin Keegan, who passed away at the age of 75 in July.

Anfield remembers Kevin Keegan ❤️A special tribute to the Liverpool legend ahead of kick-off. pic.twitter.com/bJgi58vPj7

A very poignant and colourful tribute to Kevin Keegan, with Anfield paying its respects to one of its favourite sons. The atmosphere is good and the onus is on the team to maintain it. This won’t be easy, as Nottingham Forest arrive here with a point to prove under Oliver Glasner. The big story with Forest will come later, with their pursuit of Everton’s Harrison Armstrong. It it is a transfer that is causing huge discussion on Merseyside.

Both sets of players are out onto the pitch and are met by an electric atmosphere at Anfield.

All set for #LIVNFO 💪 pic.twitter.com/IJOZ6NwGNW

Earlier this month, Liverpool owners Fenway Sports Group announced they had agreed to sell a minority equity stake to 1892 Holdings, a consortium led and managed by Amit Bhatia, who is in attendance at Anfield today.

On the development, Bhatia told Liverpool’s website: “It feels incredible. It feels surreal when I hear those words, obviously an incredibly proud moment for myself, for my family, for our partners. We’re talking about Liverpool Football Club here, right? I mean, we’re talking about the greatest football club in the world. And so to have the ability to be involved in any capacity is a huge privilege and a huge honour.”

Having been linked to both Tottenham Hotspur and Manchester City, Cody Gakpo’s Liverpool future has looked doubtful at points this summer.

However, Spurs’ signings of Savinho and Omar Marmoush, as well as Manchester City’s potentially big-money pursuit of Enzo Fernandez, means that any exit for the Dutchman looks extremely complicated.

Gakpo scored Liverpool’s first equaliser in their chaotic 2-2 draw with Newcastle United and starts today on the left wing.

❤️ https://t.co/MgbTcQWank pic.twitter.com/DwIooN2OFk

In September 2024, Nottingham Forest claimed their first win over Liverpool at Anfield in 55 years thanks to Callum Hudson-Odoi’s sumptuous 72nd-minute curler.

When Callum Hudson-Odoi made history at Anfield 🤩 pic.twitter.com/HhJ73WztMd

Last season’s emphatic 3-0 victory in the same fixture under Sean Dyche means that Forest have successive wins at a ground where they could notoriously never manage three points.

Nottingham Forest have smashed their club-record transfer fee to sign Chelsea striker Liam Delap for £50m on a five-year deal, ending a lengthy pursuit by both the club and their head coach Oliver Glasner.

Last summer Delap held talks with Forest and Glasner, while he was in charge at Crystal Palace, before he opted to join his mentor and former Manchester City Under-21 coach Enzo Maresca at Stamford Bridge.

One of the summer’s most talked about and protracted transfer pursuits is nearing its conclusion as Liverpool have agreed a £120m deal with Paris St-Germain to sign Bradley Barcola.

The Frenchman was absent from PSG’s squad on Friday evening as Luis Enrique’s side drew 2-2 with Lille in Ligue 1.

Barcola is yet another big-money addition to Liverpool’s forward line, following on from the signings of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Hugo Ekitike last summer.

He also has the approval of club legend Steven Gerrard, who is at Anfield on duty for TNT Sports.

Lining up at Liverpool. 📋 pic.twitter.com/1gtQ7BQz5J

Andoni Iraola has made two changes to the side that drew with Newcastle United. Victor Munoz starts with Rio Ngumoha on the bench. The other alteration sees Alexis Mac Allister replace Ryan Gravenberch in midfield.

Team news is IN! 🔴 #LIVNFO pic.twitter.com/3avoOQOPrM

Anfield will host its first Premier League match of the 2026-27 season.

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League match between Liverpool and Nottingham Forest at Anfield.

This encounter pits two summer appointments – Andoni Iraola and Oliver Glasner – against each other as they both search for their first top-flight win at their new clubs.

In the opening Premier League game-week, Iraola’s Liverpool needed a last-gasp 99th-minute penalty from Dominik Szoboszlai to rescue an unconvincing 2-2 draw with Newcastle United at St. James’ Park. Meanwhile, Nottingham Forest have suffered back-to-back home defeats in four days against Leeds United without scoring (1-0 Premier League, 2-0 Carabao Cup).

Iraola has been handed the unenviable task of steering Liverpool back on track following a hugely disappointing campaign under Arne Slot, whose side’s defence of their Premier League ended in a meek fifth-place finish despite spending more than £400m in the previous summer.

The former Bournemouth boss must uncover how to get the best out of big-money recruits such as Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Milos Kerkez and Jeremie Frimpong, and also tighten up Liverpool’s vulnerable midfield and defence. Given the pressure of the job and the club’s hectic schedule while balancing domestic and European football, it’s a tough ask. However, Liverpool have agreed a £120m deal for Paris St-Germain winger Bradley Barcola to bolster their attacking reinforcements, but the transfer hasn’t been finalised in time for today’s match.

Last season, Forest endured an equally tumultuous campaign, churning through a staggering four managers, before eventually stumbling to a 16th-place finish. Glasner has been hand-picked by owner Evangelos Marinakis to usher in an era of stability and success, after winning the FA Cup, Community Shield and Conference League in just over two years at Crystal Palace.

Both Marinakis and Glasner are extremely ambitious and demanding figures. You’d imagine a top-half finish would be considered the absolute minimum for Forest, while Glasner’s track record of winning trophies surely indicates that Marinakis is eyeing some silverware at the City Ground.

It’s a meeting of two managers who must deliver. Three points for either side would serve as a much-needed tonic to kickstart their seasons.

Kick-off is at 12:30, with team news coming shortly.

#1915. Report: ‘Tension is rising’ – Milan unhappy with Toulouse’s treatment of Odogu

Tension is rising between the RedBird-owned clubs AC Milan and Toulouse, according to a report, as David Odogu is yet to play a single minute this season.

In the summer, Milan sent several players out on loan, including a couple that they felt could get more playing elsewhere to then come back even stronger. Zachary Athekame springs to mind amid his great success at Lyon, but it hasn’t been as good for everyone.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Odogu, who left to join Toulouse, is yet to play a single minute for his new club. It’s rather strange as the youngster actually looked quite good in pre-season, while he got some playing time for Milan’s first team last season as well.

According to LesViolets, a website dedicated solely to Toulouse, ‘tension is rising’ between the French club and Milan, who loaned out their player with the expectation of at least semi-consistent playing time. Certainly not zero minutes after ten games.

As a result, Milan are looking for a new destination for Odogu and Toulouse aren’t counting on the German defender for the second half of the season. In other words, a loan move is more or less nailed on to happen in January.

It’s a rather strange situation as Toulouse, in case you didn’t know, is also owned by Gerry Cardinale and RedBird. It does show autonomy, which is good in a sense, but Milan were hoping to do more loan deals with the French side in the future. Perhaps not anymore.

It remains to be seen where Odogu will end up next, but in the summer, Anderlecht and Mainz also expressed an interest.

#1914. Carlton Cole says Man Utd star should have been sold years ago: ‘He’s won the lottery!’

Carlton Cole says Diogo Dalot ‘won the lottery’ when he joined Manchester United and should have been sold years ago.

Dalot is one of the United’s longest-serving players, having made over 250 appearances for the Red Devils since his £19m move from Porto in 2018.

Former Manchester United boss Jose Mourinho hailed Dalot as the ‘best young full-back in Europe’ at the time but the Portugal international has attracted much criticism during his time at Old Trafford.

Dalot has endured a particularly poor couple of weeks, struggling in United’s Champions League win over Roma and Sunday’s 4-4 draw with Aston Villa in the Premier League.

The 27-year-old was branded ‘atrocious’ after the Roma clash and was booed as he was subbed off by Michael Carrick against Villa.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Ex-England striker Cole is shocked Dalot is still at Manchester United and says the full-back ‘probably can’t believe his luck’.

‘It’s got to be down to Michael Carrick as well,’ Cole said on The Dressing Room podcast when discussing the huge issues at Old Trafford.

‘He’s playing certain personnel in that team that I’m thinking, “how are you even still there?” I’ve said it before but Diogo Dalot, how is he still there?

‘He’s way off it, he is way off it. You can’t depend on him. All he’s thinking about is his next pay check, that’s what’s going through his head.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘He’s not worried about saving the gaffer’s job. He probably can’t believe his luck that he’s there, he’s playing at Old Trafford in front of those brilliant fans in a lovely stadium with all that history.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘For me, he’s won the lottery. I don’t know how he’s on that pitch. He keeps making the same mistakes and getting caught out, he was at fault last week and he was at fault again at the weekend.’

Manchester United fans cheered when Carrick prepared to sub off Dalot against Aston Villa and then booed as he made his way off the pitch.

Asked about that reaction after the game, Carrick said: ‘We’ve got to be careful with that, I think. I understand the frustration. I understand the disappointment of the supporters, so I get it.

‘We’re all frustrated. We’re all disappointed. And the players are as much as anyone, I guarantee you that.

‘Diogo gives absolutely everything. He’s played in different positions. He’s played left-back. He’s played really well at times. He gives a penalty away today. That’s, you know… he knows that.

‘Maybe he can do a little bit better. Alright, that’s part of it, he’s made a mistake. But he cares an awful lot, and he’s given everything.

‘So I like what he brings to the team. I like what he brings to the group. I like what he brings to the whole environment and the culture that we’ve got.

‘Picking the team and who plays the next game, that’s a whole different decision. But it’s a whole different game that we’ve got to look forward to now.’

An eighth league game without a win leaves Manchester United 18th in the Premier League going into the November international break.

A dismal start to the 2026/27 campaign looks set to cost Carrick his job at Old Trafford, with Eddie Howe the current frontrunner to take over.

#1913. Dave Challinor: I've seen everyone now ahead of first League One game as Sheffield Wednesday manager

All that was up for grabs between the Owls and Accrington Stanley on Tuesday was which team would have a home tie in the last-32 as group winners, and it was the League Two side who took it with a 4-0 win.

Wednesday used the opportunity to protect senior players, having a debut to Louis Poland and substitute James Kay, plus a first start to Denny Oliver.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

It showed in a disjointed performance in only Challinor's second game in charge, the first being Sunday's FA Cup exit at the hands of League Two Oldham Athletic.

"I suppose it's what I expected really, the one thing it has done it means I've seen pretty much every player over the time I've been at the club in terms of first-team fixtures, youth-team fixtures, and a mixture today," he said. "But understanding of where priorities were and what was most important.

"Some young players have made their debuts and it was a really proud moment for them and things that they'll remember.

"Obviously the challenges which there's going to be but for all of them they should be better for the experience whether it's good or bad and should stand them in good stead hopefully moving forward on the start of their journeys."

With only 5,472 in attendance at Hillsborough on a cold night and no real jeopardy, the match was played in a subdued atmosphere.

"It's tough because it almost becomes like a pre-season game really where you're expecting there to be little cohesion because you're chucking a group together that don't train together on separate sites, put together really last minute in terms of what it looked like," said Challinor. "It was probably making decisions on some players even within the group we've got whether they're able and some injuries.

"We had to make structured substitutions so I went into it not expecting loads, understanding what it would look like and probably you have to get yourself in that headspace as early as possible so as not to become frustrated because young players especially are going to make mistakes. Some of the more senior ones in terms of minutes and football are still very young and still make mistakes.

"That was probably what the game looked like from our perspective. To run through a few that may or may not be on the fringes of the first team."

One big plus for George Brown was his first appearance of an injury-hit 2026, leading the line before making way at half-time.

"It was a tough comeback for him because an experienced centre-half who's been round the block and we played pretty direct into him.

"We told Connal (Trueman, the goalkeeper) if it was on to play, play, but can we play over, especially for the young lads early on and try and get them a feel. George had a right fight on his hands but he's got through 45 minutes which is brilliant."

Sean Fusire captained the side from right wing-back, but will miss Saturday's League One game at home to Plymouth Argyle on international duty with Zimbabwe.

"He hasn't got the vaccinations to go to Equatorial Guinea," where Zimbabwe play on Thursday. "The plan is I think he travels tomorrow (Thursday) for the game on Sunday (the reverse fixture in the African Cup of Nations qualifiers), and Kieran (Morrison) and Jordi (Liongola) are away as well."

#1912. 'Winning at the Emirates is very hard... but we were a team of warriors': Hull City hero GEOVANNI on his iconic goal against Arsenal, why it very nearly never happened and why the Tigers 'will always be in my heart'

Published: 21:00 EST, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 06:07 EST, 7 November 2026

The greatest moment in Hull City's Premier League history began with Geovanni trying to go home.

'I was ill all night, I barely slept at all,' says Geovanni, who was gripped by a fever and thumping headache less than 24 hours before he was due to walk out at Arsenal's Emirates Stadium in September 2008. The Brazilian rang his wife from the team hotel to tell her he was coming home and planned to have someone pick him up.

Thankfully, his wife Roberta would not hear of it.

'God really used her that day,' he tells Daily Mail Sport. 'She said: "Geovanni, stay there, God will honour you. Hang on and tomorrow try to get a bit of sleep."'

When Hull staff came to his room the next morning, he asked to be left to sleep. He dosed up on medicine and went for lunch, but sat out the light pre-match training session with his temperature touching 38 degrees Celsius.

'And then I got to that game, which was so spectacular,' he says, 'and I was able to score and help Hull beat Arsenal.'

Geovanni unleashes a spectacular equaliser for Hull at the Emirates Stadium back in September 2008

The goal inspired a famous comeback win for the Tigers, who became only the second team to win away at Arsenal

It was Hull's first league meeting with Arsenal for 93 years, in the first top-flight season of the club's then 104-year history.

Arsene Wenger's side had started the day top of the table and Paul McShane's own goal put Arsenal ahead after 51 minutes. Most expected the floodgates to open.

But 11 minutes later up stepped Hull's brilliant Brazilian, a marquee signing from Manchester City in the summer of 2008 after the Tigers' unexpected promotion.

Geovanni cut inside Theo Walcott and sent a 25-yard rocket into Manuel Almunia's top corner. Daniel Cousin headed in a historic winner four minutes later and Hull became only the second side to beat Arsenal at the Emirates.

'Beating Arsenal at the Emirates is very hard, and we pulled it off,' says Geovanni, now 46, speaking from his home in Brazil. 'That was a team of warriors, great players, and we had a really good friendship. And that day we walked away with a great win.'

On Saturday, Hull return to the Emirates to face the champions and league leaders. The Tigers are 11th after nine games. It is a strong start that few predicted.

'Hull have to give 100 per cent, the maximum, be switched on the whole time,' says Geovanni. 'It's difficult, but it's not impossible, because Hull really did beat Arsenal.'

Eight days after the Emirates match, Geovanni did it again. A stunning 30-yard free-kick at White Hart Lane nestled into the top corner past his friend and compatriot Heurelho Gomes.

'We beat Tottenham with Gareth Bale, Luka Modric, all those players,' he says. 'For me, those two are top-drawer. They're two great players who left a mark on me.'

The win moved Hull into third and by the end of October they were level on points at the top. 'London 0 Hull 2' read the headline in the local paper, in reference to Hull band The Housemartins' 1986 album London 0 Hull 4, as the city revelled in its newfound fame.

Geovanni (centre) was part of another iconic Premier League moment, when Phil Brown gave his team a public dressing down at half-time of a loss at Manchester City

The Brazilian returned to Hull's MKM Stadium last year and received a hero's welcome

Geovanni took centre stage. Arriving on a free that summer after being released by Manchester City, he credits manager Phil Brown and assistant Brian Horton for giving him a second chance in the Premier League.

'They were very special people in allowing me to stay in England, which was my dream,' he says. 'And I learned a lot from both of them. Brian was a very experienced coach, he played for Hull, he managed there, so the affection and respect are huge. Whenever I can talk about them, I do.

'In the first year, Hull surprised a lot of people precisely because of the way we played. Sometimes we'd start in a 4-3-1-2, I played as the No10 behind two strikers. And if we were struggling to mark, I'd drop in to close down the left flank and we'd go back to a 4-4-2.'

The dressing room did the rest. Richard Garcia, an Australian winger with Uruguayan parents, helped translate team talks from English into Spanish and captain Ian Ashbee, Nicky Barmby and Bernard Mendy all made Geovanni feel welcome. 'I'm really happy about the friendships I made in that dressing room,' he says.

Geovanni was part of another of the Premier League's most iconic moments, when he and his team-mates received a public dressing down from his manager on the pitch at half-time of a 5-1 loss to Manchester City on Boxing Day 2008. Eleven months later, Jimmy Bullard scored a penalty before recreating the telling off in celebration.

'It was good for breaking the ice,' says Geovanni. 'From that day on the atmosphere got better too, because we can all make mistakes. The most important thing is to admit the mistake and move on.'

Geovanni's finest moment for Manchester City, with whom he spent one season after stints with Barcelona, Benfica and Cruzeiro, came in the Manchester derby, where he was called into the side by manager Sven-Goran Eriksson because Stephen Ireland was ill.

'He called me over and said, "Geovanni, this game... are you ready?". That was the best news I'd had all day, knowing I was going to start.' The day did, in fact, get better. Geovanni scored the only goal in a 1-0 victory.

Geovanni smashes home a winner for City in the Manchester derby, a year before his move to Hull

United were a familiar victim. In December 2005, his diving header for Benfica helped knock Sir Alex Ferguson's side out of the Champions League in the group stages

He struck again against United in November 2008, in a 4-3 defeat for Hull at Old Trafford

United were a familiar victim. In December 2005, his diving header for Benfica helped knock Sir Alex Ferguson's side out of the Champions League in the group stages, while he also scored in a 4-3 defeat for Hull at Old Trafford in 2008.

'A player has to turn up in the big games,' he says. 'United were a machine back then: Giggs, Paul Scholes, Gary Neville, Anderson, Ronaldo, Rooney.'

Geovanni's greatest regret, though, remains that he didn't heed the advice of Barca boss Louis van Gaal, who wanted to turn the wannabe striker into a wing-back.

He reflects: 'If I could go back in time, I'd listen to what Van Gaal said, because it would have been easier for me to fight for a place at wing-back than as a striker, where there were great players: Javier Saviola, Rivaldo, Patrick Kluivert, Marc Overmars.'

Luiz Felipe Scolari, his coach at Cruzeiro, gave him his only senior Brazil cap, against Mexico at the 2001 Copa America. 'It was a dream for me: to leave a town of 4,000 people (Acaiaca) and one day represent Brazil,' he says. 'He (Scolari) was a father to me.'

These days Geovanni is a volunteer pastor in Belo Horizonte and runs a players' agency with his father-in-law and an old youth-team friend.

But Hull will always be in his heart. He has a picture of himself in a Hull shirt in his house and received a hero's return after heading back to the city last year.

'I love them (the fans). I have a very special affection for the Hull supporters,' he says. 'It was two years in which I gave everything. I went back there last year and was really well received, it was great: friends from my time there, the fans too.

Battling Blackburn's Damien Duff in a pre-season friendly in his Barcelona days. He spent only two seasons with the Catalan club, having left Cruzeiro to move to Europe

'I'm very grateful for everything they did for me. Hull and the fans will always be in my heart'

'And I know I left my mark on the club's history. Whenever people talk about Hull City, about Brazilians, they'll remember Geovanni, the time I spent there, the feats we achieved together.

'And I believe I gave those fans a lot of joy, in games that seemed impossible. God blessed me and I was able to score goals and bring joy to that city. I'm very grateful for everything they did for me. Hull and the fans will always be in my heart.

'My two years at Hull were perhaps the two most special years for me. The sweetest spell of my career.'

#1911. William Gallas says only one team can rival Arsenal for the Premier League title

William Gallas believes that only one team has the ability to rival Arsenal in this season’s Premier League title race.

Arsenal are now five points clear at the top of the league table following their hard-fought 1-0 win at home to Hull City on Saturday.

But it was another bad weekend for Manchester City as their third successive league defeat saw Enzo Maresca’s side slip to third.

Brighton are now second in the table as Fabian Hurzeler’s side continued their superb start to the season with a 2-0 win over Brentford.

The Seagulls have already beaten both Arsenal and City in the league this season, with no team scoring more goals and only Arsenal conceding fewer after ten games.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

But despite that impressive start from Brighton, Gallas still expects City to come on strong and provide the only real test for Arsenal in the title race this campaign.

‘It will be very interesting to see if they can maintain that performance until the end of the season, but we know the second part is always the most difficult time for any club,’ Gallas told Tribal Football.

‘Right now, it looks like only those two teams, Arsenal and Manchester City, are really going to fight for the title.’

Gallas was also keen to rave about Arsenal’s superb defensive record once again this season, adding: ‘They have conceded just five goals, and that is going to be the question from everyone: how many goals will they concede this season?

‘Last season, I know everybody was talking about them conceding maybe less than 15 goals, but in the second part of the season, it was difficult for Arsenal. Right now, they look really, really strong.

#1910. Serie A preview: Genoa vs. AC Milan – Team news, opposition insight, stats and prediction

A tough away trip awaits AC Milan on Sunday afternoon, hoping to restore some order against an in-form Genoa side.

What many hoped would be a positive week quickly turned into a negative one, as Milan failed to build on the derby win against Ferencvaros. In other words, they need to respond with a strong performance against Genoa, which is easier said than done.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Ruben Amorim didn’t have a press conference earlier today due to the tight schedule, so there are no new takeaways from him. Judging from the post-match interviews on Thursday, however, he’s expecting a lot more from his players at the Marassi.

Game date: Sunday, November 8 Kick-off time: 15:00 (CET) Venue: Stadio Luigi Ferraris Referee: Davide Massa (VAR: Camplone)

It’s been said for quite a few games now, but Amorim certainly isn’t being helped by the injury situation. In total, seven players will be on the sidelines for the game tomorrow, including key players like Samuel Chukwueze, Strahinja Pavlovic and Alexis Saelemaekers.

Milan were hoping to recover the Serbian for this one, but severe stomach pain is keeping him on the sidelines after missing the Ferencvaros game too. Considering that Matteo Gabbia and Fikayo Tomori were already on the injury list, it’s certainly not ideal.

Mike Maignan will be back between the sticks, at least, after serving a suspension in the Europa League. He will have a defence of Mario Gila, Koni De Winter, Sankhoun Diawara and Pervis Estupinan ahead of him, with the left flank being the main worry there.

In midfield, Ardon Jashari will be demoted to the bench as Luka Modric will be back from start, partnering with Yunus Musah in a tandem. Adrien Rabiot, meanwhile, is expected to have a slightly more advanced role.

Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic will be the danger men on the attacking flanks, looking to replicate their success against Inter in the derby. The same cannot be said for Goncalo Ramos, who instead needs to get going with his goalscoring after bagging just two league goals so far.

In terms of firepower on the bench, Amorim could turn to Davide Bartesaghi, the aforementioned Jashari, Omari Hutchinson and Alphadjo Cisse. Francesco Camarda will also be there, of course, but whether he can be categorised as an impact player is a different question.

Predicted Milan XI (4-2-3-1): Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Diawara, Estupinan; Musah, Modric; Moreira, Rabiot, Pulisic; Ramos.

Predicted bench: Torriani, Bouyer, F. Terracciano, Vladimirov, Bartesaghi, Jashari, Comotto, Hutchinson, Cisse, Camarda.

Injuries & suspensions: Chukwueze, Gabbia, Loftus-Cheek, Pavlovic, Saelemaekers, Terracciano, Tomori.

After what was a disastrous start to the 2025-26 season under Patrick Vieira, sitting rock bottom between the 7th and 9th matchdays, Daniele De Rossi was appointed. He quickly brought them above the relegation zone and managed to keep them there, finishing seven points clear in the end.

It was only right to confirm him for this season, as such, and there have been no regrets so far. The start was admittedly dodgy, with one draw and four defeats in the first five games, but there have been four wins and one defeat in the five games since. Crisis very much averted.

The only defeat in the last five games came against De Rossi’s former club as well, namely Roma, who have been on fire at the start of this season. There can be no accusations of the former midfielder throwing the game to benefit his former club, let’s put it that way.

Nevertheless, the poor star has been cancelled out and it’s possible that De Rossoneri just needed some time, especially after losing key players like Jeff Ekhator (to Juventus) and Brooke Norton-Vuffy (to Hull City). The Serie A veteran Ruslan Malinovskyi also waved goodbye as his contract expired.

On the flip side, the Rossoblu did keep hold of most of the key players from last season, such as Johan Vasquez, Leo Ostigard, Morten Frendrup, and Lorenzo Colombo. The latter was signed permanently from Milan after a season-long loan, as the conditions for the obligation were triggered.

Some interesting signings were also made, from the veteran (and former Milan man) Stephan El Shaarawy to the familiar face Hamed Traore, who played for Sassuolo between 2019 and 2013. After spells at Bournemouth, Napoli, Auxerre and Marseille, he’s now looking to regain stability.

As for the latest team news, De Rossi has a much better situation than Amorim with no injuries or suspensions to note. Lorenzo Venturino and Elias Havel were both on the sidelines but have returned for this one.

It looks like the former Milan men El Shaarawy and Colombo will start, while Junior Messias could perhaps be introduced from the bench. De Rossi didn’t give much away during his presser in terms of the team selection, but he did make it clear that Genoa cannot get too cocky.

Genoa (3-5-2): Bijlow; Marcandalli, Ostigard, Vasquez; Ellertsson, Baldanzi, Frendrup, Traore, El Shaarawy; Colombo, Osmajic.

Predicted bench: Stolz, Sommariva, Messias, Otoa, Sabelli, Puczka, Amorim, Meichtry, Mitaj, Vitinha, Sow, Drameh, Ehizibue, Wiafe, Venturino, Havel.

This will be the 157th encounter between the two sides, with Milan looking to build on their 71 wins in the fixture, while Genoa are quite far behind at 37 wins. 48 games have ended all square, which is a tally that has increased lately.

In the last five games, there have been three draws (3-3, 0-0 and 1-1), but the good news for the Rossoneri is that they won the other two games. The five games before that were all wins as well, with no defeat recorded against the Rossoblu since 2020.

The most recent win was a 2-1 win at the Marassi in favour of Milan, courtesy of goals from Christopher Nkunku and Zachary Athekame. They both left the club on loan this summer, so they won’t be of any help tomorrow.

In the game before that, Rafael Leao (another player who’s no longer in the team) rescued a point in the dying minutes after Colombo had given Genoa the lead in the first half.

➤ Milan are unbeaten in their last 10 Serie A matches against Genoa (W6 D4). Since 2020-21, the Rossoneri only have a longer run of unbeaten games against Hellas Verona (12).

➤ Milan have won each of their last four Serie A away games against Genoa; only against three teams do the Rossoneri currently have a longer running away win streak in the competition: Hellas Verona (seven), Messina (five) and Pisa (five).

➤ Genoa are on a three-game winning streak in Serie A. The last time the Rossoblu recorded a streak of four consecutive wins in a single season in the top flight was between March and April 2009.

➤ Genoa have won three of their first six home games this season (D1 L2). The Rossoblu haven’t won four of their first seven Serie A home games since the 2015-16 season, when Gian Piero Gasperini was in charge.

➤ Ruben Amorim’s Milan have scored 21 goals in their first 10 Serie A games this season. The last Rossoneri manager to do better after his first 11 league games was Cesare Maldini in 1972, with 25 goals.

➤ Milan have won two and drawn three of their first five away games this season. The Rossoneri have avoided defeat in their first six away games of the season on three occasions between 2020-21 and 2025-26, the same number as Inter and Napoli, and could now become the only team to do so four times in this span, including the current season.

➤ Genoa have scored four goals in the first 15 minutes of Serie A action this season, a figure they share with Frosinone, Atalanta, Lazio, and Roma and second only to Milan (five). However, the Rossoblu are the only team yet to score in the final 15 minutes of a match.

➤ Stephan El Shaarawy, who scored 21 goals in 83 league appearances for AC Milan, has provided an assist in each of his last two Serie A appearances. Should he also contribute to a goal in his next match, he would become, at 34 years and 12 days, the second-oldest player to achieve this feat in three consecutive games for Genoa since 2004-05, after Domenico Criscito in 2021 (34 years and 269 days).

➤ Adrien Rabiot has bagged five goals and three assists in his first eight league appearances this season. The last midfielder to do better in the first nine games of a Serie A season was Sergej Milinkovic-Savic in 2022-23, with 10 contributions (three goals and seven assists).

Furthermore, the Frenchman has been involved in a goal in each of his last five appearances, and the last Milan midfielder to do better in Serie A was Kaka in 2004 (seven).

➤ Diego Moreira has been directly involved in seven goals (four goals and three assists) in his first six Serie A appearances for AC Milan. Since 2004/05, no player has had more in his first six league games for the Rossoneri, equaling Mario Balotelli’s record (seven in 2013).

Starting with Milan, and at the back, I think we should keep an extra eye on Diawara. He did well in the derby but after switching to centre-back for the Ferencvaros game, his display just wasn’t good enough. He will have the same position tomorrow and we need to see an improvement.

Further up the pitch, Moreira showed in the derby that he can be just the X-factor that Milan need, and this game should be an even better one for him (at least on paper). The cameo against Ferencvaros was positive despite the result, so hopefully he can build on the last week.

As for the home side, I’m curious to see Traore in action again. He definitely had some very good games for Sassuolo against the Rossoneri and with more consistent playing time at Genoa, he could rediscover that spark which made him so special.

Finally, I think it would be silly to ignore the defensive general, Vasquez. He always seems to have good games against Milan and honestly, he’s the type of player the Rossoneri could use right now, at least as a deputy.

It’s been incredibly hard to predict how well Milan will do so far this season, with many ups and downs. However, my gut feeling tells me that they will be able to do a whole lot better than on Thursday, especially since the key players are back from start.

My only worry is the left-hand side of the defence, with Diawara and Estupinan set to start there. As such, I’m going to go for a narrow win, with no clean sheet either. Let us know your prediction in the comments below!

Team must go for the win because this season and today position is opening opportunity to reach top positions.

Milan will win this game but again depend on the rotation. Personally I think why Milan can’t play consistently because of the heavily rotation. You cant gel into the games if too many changes each every game. They should just change 1 or two every game. Even when you want to rest certain key players. Just substitute them by half time instead.

#1909. Martin Zubimendi responds to Chelsea transfer speculation and reveals Mikel Arteta warning

Martin Zubimend has revealed he was warned he would face a fight to maintain his status as a regular starter at Arsenal this season, but insists he hasn’t given up hope of winning back his place.

The Spain international joined the Gunners 18 months ago following a £60million move from Real Sociedad.

Zubimendi had come close to signing for Liverpool a year earlier, but was convinced to snub the Reds’ interest and delay a move to England, with Mikel Arteta outlining his determination to make him a key component of his midfield rebuild.

The 27-year-old’s decision to move to the north London club initially looked an inspired one as he played almost every game over the course of the first two thirds of a campaign that ultimately ended in glory.

Fatigue, however, eventually caught up with Zubimendi and his place was effectively taken by teenager Myles Lewis-Skelly during the run-in and he has been reduced to a bit-part role ever since.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Arsenal’s decision to sanction the signing of Bruno Guimaraes has only served to further heighten the intense competition for places and, as a result, Zubimendi is yet to start a Premier League game this season.

That lack of game time has sparked intense speculation that a January move could be on the cards for the World Cup winner.

Chelsea, who are in the market for a midfielder and whose manager, Xabi Alonso, attempted to sign Zubimendi during his brief stint in charge of Real Madrid, are said to be considering renewing interest having made tentative enquiries during the summer.

Atletico Madrid, meanwhile, have been positioned as the frontrunners, with Diego Simeone said to be dreaming of signing the Arsenal star with reports in Spain going as far as saying that a deal is close.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Responding to a whirlwind of rumours, Zubimendi told Marca: ‘To be honest, I’m sometimes surprised by the press too. I understand that the winter transfer window is approaching and rumors can surface, but I think we need to be a bit more careful with what we publish.

‘Ultimately, everyone has a team they play for, and we need to respect that. I’ve also read that I might be close, but not at all.

‘Often a news story comes out and it seems that if it doesn’t come true, it’s quickly forgotten and nothing happens. I’m learning how this world works and getting used to it, but sometimes I could avoid a lot of the messages I receive because of this kind of news.’

Asked whether his current predicament has come as a surprise, Zubimendi revealed Arteta had been totally transparent at the season’s outset and outlined the role he envisaged for a player he fought so hard to sign.

He said:  ‘I spoke with Mikel at the beginning of the season. As he does with all the players, he explained the plan to me.

‘He warned me that there were new signings and that there would be playing time for everyone. And here we are, fighting for it.

‘I understand because, for me, we’re among the five best teams in Europe. There are some fantastic players. New signings have arrived in my position, and there were already some very good players. I’m also part of that competition that makes it so difficult to get playing time.’

He added:  ‘I’m calm and happy with how I’m handling this situation. It’s something I’ve never experienced before, and I think you learn from these situations too.

‘Besides, it’s in moments like these that you need the people around you the most, and they’re there for you.

‘I’m patient. When you’ve been playing a lot of minutes and your role changes to not playing as much, I’m able to see the positive side. I think everything passes, that just like last year the opposite happened to me and I played practically everything, this can change very quickly.’

#1908. Manchester United finalising deal to appoint Michael Carrick’s replacement

Manchester United are close to rubber stamping a deal to appoint Michael Carrick’s successor ahead of making a final decision on the future of their current head coach.

The Red Devils are languishing in the relegation zone after Sunday’s chaotic 4-4 draw with Aston Villa which is expected to represent Carrick’s final game at the helm, despite an injury-time comeback which yielded an unlikely point.

Carrick currently remains in limbo and attended United’s training ground on Wednesday morning with club executives set to discuss his future at a meeting in Monaco.

The 45-year-old was photographed driving into the club’s Carrington base this morning, but his fate is set to be determined at a meeting 800 miles away, where co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe will confer with United chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox.

According to the Athletic, United’s key decision makers held talks on Tuesday and settled on Mauricio Pochettino as the candidate best qualified to lead the club out of the almost unprecedented mess it finds itself in.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager signed a contract with US Soccer through to 2030 just three months ago, and is currently preparing the American national side for CONCACAF Nations League matches against Haiti in the November international break.

The former Argentina international has held talks with United in the past and is keen on the job this time, but hefty compensation would be due to US Soccer.

United are understood to have been in contact with Pochettino’s representatives and although personal terms are unlikely to be an issue, the 54-year-old’s exit clause of £7.4million would need to be paid in full.

Aston Villa boss Unai Emery is admired, while ex-Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and former Germany head coach Julian Nagelsmann were linked a fortnight ago when United seriously considered replacing Carrick.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

A 4-1 Champions League loss at Como and 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth left the head coach’s job hanging by a thread, but the club decided to give him the opportunity to turn the situation around.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Carrick’s side subsequently lost 2-0 at Chelsea, where they were unable to take their chances and saw Lisandro Martinez sent off, before last Tuesday’s thrilling 3-2 Champions League comeback win against Roma.

A scarcely believable 4-4 draw against followed on Sunday, after which the head coach stressed he would not walk away.

‘It’s been a right mixed week or two or three, really, if you’re looking at the events,’ Carrick said. ‘But I’m pretty clear where we need to go and how we need to get there.

‘Obviously some of the boys will be flying off around the world and different things, and the group will be split for 10 days or so.

‘But as a normal international week is, you know, we’ll have some training. We’ll have one or two days off, but not too much. But we’ll train, and we’ll get ready for the next game.’

United return to action with a Premier League trip to rivals Liverpool on November 22.

#1907. Arsenal dealt transfer blow in pursuit of Mikel Arteta’s ‘top target’

Bournemouth have ruled out a transfer move for rumoured Arsenal target Eli Junior Kroupi this January.

Arsenal scoured the market for attacking reinforcements in the summer transfer window, with Mikel Arteta keen to add firepower to his title-winning frontline.

Christos Tzolis was signed for a fee of £34million from Club Brugge to help fill the void left by the departure of both Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli – and the Greece international has gone on to enjoy an encouraging start to life in north London.

However, it was clear the Premier League champions had ideally intended to bring in another proven talent in this area of the pitch after the club were gazumped by Chelsea in the race for Morgan Rogers.

There was genuine interest in Vinicius Junior and the Gunners were reportedly hopeful of closing a deal for the Real Madrid superstar right up until the start of August.

But Vinicius would go on to pen a new long-term contract at the Bernabeu, ultimately leaving Arsenal disappointed in their efforts to provide support and competition for the likes of Noni Madueke, Bukayo Saka, Kai Havertz, Viktor Gyokeres and Tzolis.

According to talkSPORT, Arsenal are ready to reenter the transfer market to land a top-class attacker this winter and have a number of high-profile names on their shortlist of possible solutions.

It’s claimed Endrick, Vinicius’ team-mate at both club and international level, is now firmly on Arsenal’s radar after failing to win over Jose Mourinho at Madrid.

Kroupi has racked up 13 goals and one assist in 39 appearances for Bournemouth and is widely regarded to be among the most exciting young talents in Premier League football.

Arsenal will likely fall short should their step up their pursuit of Kroupi this January, though, as the Cherries are said to have ‘made it clear’ that the 20-year-old is not for sale.

The France Under-21 international underwent surgery for a foot injury back in July and made his return to first-team action as a late substitute in Bournemouth’s stunning 3-0 victory at Manchester United last month.

Marco Rose is still yet to start Kroupi this season but the former Lorient man has also featured as a substitute in Bournemouth’s recent wins over Aston Villa, Leeds and Ipswich.

The versatile forward has three-and-a-half years remaining on his current contract at the Vitality Stadium.

Last season, Kroupi scored the goal against Manchester City that ultimately sealed Arsenal’s status as champions after a painful 22-year wait for the title.

Asked if he’d been congratulated by any thankful Arsenal players at the time, he told Stadium Astro: ‘Yes I have received many messages but I tell myself that I didn’t do this for Arsenal.

‘I do this for Bournemouth. I can say I scored against Arsenal, I scored against City.

‘It doesn’t change anything, I just wanted to help my team.’

When asked about his goals and ambitions for the future, Kroupi replied: ‘Perform with my team and perform also in Europe also because it is very beautiful to be in Europe but you have to perform to play there.’

#1906. 'I want to win the Ballon d'Or': JJ Gabriel sets out his lofty ambitions as Man United wonderkid, 16, closes in on move to Real Madrid after quitting Red Devils

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 06:08 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 06:09 EST, 7 November 2026

Manchester United wonderkid JJ Gabriel has revealed his ambition to win the Ballon d'Or as he dropped the clearest hint yet that he is heading to Real Madrid in an interview with Spanish media.

The 16-year-old sensation stunned Manchester United with a formal transfer request in September and is now on the verge of finalising his move to the Spanish capital.

Daily Mail Sport exclusively revealed Madrid's growing confidence in securing the free-scoring starlet last month, with Gabriel now having secured a European Union passport through his mother's Cypriot heritage.

The youngster, who is currently working with a personal trainer in Madrid, practically confirmed the transfer in an interview with Spanish newspaper Marca on Friday night, admitting he had a clear preference to Real over archrivals Barcelona.

'Obviously Madrid,' Gabriel told the outlet when asked which LaLiga giant he preferred.

According to the newspaper, who expects his move to be finalised in January, Gabriel's response prompted a laugh from his father and mentor Joe O'Cearuill.

Manchester United prodigy JJ Gabriel poses for his interview with Spanish newspaper Marca

Gabriel is set to complete a move to Real Madrid after formally requesting to leave Old Trafford

'My dream is to win the Ballon d'Or,' explained the talented youngster, who scored a hat-trick for Manchester United in the UEFA Youth League just days before submitting his transfer request.

Although Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe and Barcelona's Lamine Yamal narrowly missed out on winning the 2026 Ballon d'Or - which was held aloft by England captain and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane - the two LaLiga giants have long had a rich association with the award, regularly producing the world's best footballer.

While sources at United insist there has been no club-to-club contact, it appears only a matter of time before Gabriel is sporting Real Madrid's iconic all-white jersey.

It is understood Gabriel will play for Madrid's Castilla team, which plays in Spain's third division, as well as in the Youth League.

Gabriel broke a series of records playing for United youth teams, including becoming the youngest player to feature in the Under-18s.

The prodigy, who was 14 when he netted twice on his debut, has also played - and scored - for Manchester United's Under-21 side.

The Red Devils were rocked in September when Gabriel and his representatives made a bombshell request to have his academy contract torn up. That request was immediately refused by United and, while there was faint hope that a compromise could have been found to keep him at Old Trafford, he has stayed away ever since.

Gabriel's dream is to win the Ballon d'Or, which was awarded this year to England's Harry Kane

As Daily Mail Sport previously reported, United's decline since the days of Sir Alex Ferguson has been the driving force behind Gabriel's family seeking an exit. United have not won a Premier League title since 2013.

A source close to the family explained that United are 'far away' from the likes of Barcelona, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich, as well as domestic rivals Arsenal and Manchester City, and that they want him to 'learn from the best' to maximise his talents.

His father has been described as a fiercely ambitious, pushy parent and is credited with the decision to get JJ out of United in an attempt to fast-track his career.

#1905. Next Man United manager: Mauricio Pochettino's USMNT release clause 'revealed' as Michael Carrick sack rumours intensify

By Ben Sully | 10 Nov 2026 00:23, Last updated: 10 Nov 2026 03:04

Manchester United-linked Mauricio Pochettino reportedly has a release clause in his contract with the US Men's National Team (USMNT).

The Man United hierarchy are expected to make a decision on Michael Carrick's future before the end of the international break.

The current belief is that Carrick will be relieved of his duties after overseeing an eight-game winless league run that has left the club languishing in the Premier League drop zone.

Mauricio Pochettino is one of the names who have been linked with the post despite extending his contract with the USA until 2030.

According to journalist Ben Jacobs, Pochettino's deal contains a release clause that could open the door to a Premier League return.

The release clause is said to be close to the $10m (£7.4m) mark, an amount that will not stop Man United from pursuing the Argentine if they feel he is the right person for the job.

Pochettino, meanwhile, is believed to be open to the job despite appearing to commit his long-term future to the USMNT.

If he were to replace Carrick, it would see him return to club management for the first time since leaving Chelsea at the end of the 2023-24 season.

Appointing someone of Pochettino's calibre would feel like an upgrade, considering Carrick's only previous managerial experience came in the Championship with Middlesbrough.

In stark contrast, Pochettino has overseen 294 Premier League games across his spells with Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea.

The 54-year-old built his reputation as a top manager during his time with Spurs, where he recorded 160 wins in 293 competitive games and notably guided the club to the 2018-19 Champions League final.

Pochettino has previously proven to be a good man-manager, and he would bring a clear philosophy that he has developed over his career, although the obvious doubt is whether his demanding, high-intensity style of play would suit the current Man United squad.
