#1822. UEFA Nations League 2026-27: How do suspensions work? Yellow and red card rules explained

By Matt Law | 10 Nov 2026 11:17, Last updated: 10 Nov 2026 11:18

The league phase of the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League will conclude in November 2026.

The League A quarter-finals, and League A/B and B/C playoffs will then take place in March 2027, ahead of the Finals in June 2027, and it is set to be a fascinating conclusion to the tournament.

However, players run the risk of suspensions for key matches.

Here, Sports Mole explains how 2026-27 Nations League suspensions work, including the rules surrounding yellow and red cards in the tournament.

In the 2026-27 Nations League, a player is automatically suspended for one match after receiving two yellow cards in separate matches during the league phase.

A second yellow in a separate match therefore equals a one-game ban, while a fourth yellow and a sixth yellow would carry further one-match suspensions.

A straight red card or two yellow cards in the same match means that the player would be automatically suspended for their next match in the tournament.

However, a straight red card can potentially result in a longer ban, depending on the seriousness of the offence, which would be looked at by UEFA.

"As a rule, a player or team official sent off by the referee is automatically suspended for the next match in the competition. In the event of a serious offence, the UEFA disciplinary bodies are entitled to augment this punishment, including by extending it to other competitions," says Article 60 of the Regulations of the UEFA Nations League.

Under the 2026-27 rules, the accumulation of yellow cards will continue from the league stage into the quarter-finals, but after the quarter-finals, the remaining yellow cards are wiped.

As a result, heading into the semi-finals and final, there will be no accumulation of previous yellow cards, so at this stage, only a red card would lead to a suspension.

#1821. Who can England face in Nations League quarter-final? Next opponents confirmed ahead of Croatia rematch

England are on course to record their best ever performance in the Nations League, having beaten the Czech Republic twice and Croatia during the autumn international break.

Including its inaugural season in 2018/19, the Three Lions have competed in every single Nations League campaign, experiencing some highs and the lowest of lows.

From topping their group and qualifying for the Nations League finals and finishing third to suffering a shock relegation in 2022/23 and then immediate promotion, England have done almost everything except win the competition.

Having started the 2026/27 campaign with a loss to Spain, despite leading 2-1 at one stage, England bounced back in style by beating the Czechs twice and then thumping Croatia 7-0 to put themselves in a great position to advance to the quarter-finals.

Whether that be as group winners or runners-up will ultimately be determined during this international break, but Thomas Tuchel’s side have positioned themselves well to qualify for the Nations League knockout stage with two games remaining.

The victory against Czech Republic at Wembley last month has practically guaranteed England a top-two finish in Nations League A, Group 3.

They are not technically into the knockout stages just yet, though, but mathematically, it is nigh-on impossible for Croatia to jump above them.

They would need to defeat the Three Lions by eight unanswered goals at Wembley on Thursday to stop Tuchel’s men progressing.

As such, England, six points clear of their rivals, can pretty much consider themselves qualified for the last eight.

The four group winners will face the four runners-up in a two-legged Nations League quarter-final.

The group winners will all be seeded and will have home advantage in their respective second leg ties. Teams from the same group cannot be paired together in the knockout stage, therefore England and Spain - for example - would be kept apart.

#1820. Genoa 1-2 AC Milan: Cisse and Pulisic score in hard-fought victory

AC Milan secured a much-needed three points on Sunday afternoon as they beat an in-form Genoa side 2-1 at the Stadio Luigi Ferraris.

The groundwork for the victory was laid in the first half, when Alphadjo Cisse slotted in a cut-back from Adrien Rabiot to get his eighth of the campaign, before Christian Pulisic buried a square pass from Gonçalo Ramos after a stray pass inside the box.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Ellertsson made it a very nervy finish for the Rossoneri with a goal inside the final few minutes from a long-range strike, but Milan did ultimately manage to hang on for what was an important three points.

It means that a top four spot has been reclaimed for the time being while waiting to see how the game between Inter and Como plays out, and it eases some of the pressure heading into the international break.

Ruben Amorim chose to make five changes from Thursday’s defeat to Ferencvaros. Mike Maignan, Mario Gila, Luka Modric, Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic all came into the side, though there were some question marks about whether it would be a four or three-man defence based on the names selected.

Genoa started on the front foot and they immediately created an opening inside the first minute. Koni De Winter allowed Osmajic to run off his shoulder and get a shot off from the left side of the box, but Maignan watched it roll narrowly wide of the far post.

One minute after Vitinha had back-heeled a near-post cross into Maignan’s hands, Milan created their first opening. Pulisic’s cross from the byline wasn’t well-aimed but the clearance fell straight to Ramos, who didn’t quite connect right with his effort and sent it a couple of yards wide of the far post.

Milan continued to knock on the door and Ramos almost found himself on the end of a golden opportunity when Gila was found on the overlap and provided a cut-back, though Marcandalli did brilliantly to cut out the danger.

Then, in the 13th minute, Milan did take the lead through Alphadjo Cisse. The goal was assisted by Adrien Rabiot who found the run of the Italian with a nice square ball, but Pulisic was the one who won possession back on the high press to create the opportunity, which was well finished by Cisse for his eighth goal of the campaign.

In the 19th minute, the Rossoneri doubled their lead. Another successful press forced Ostigard into a mistake as his square ball back towards the goalkeeper was cut off by Ramos. The Portuguese squared to Pulisic after evading a defender, and the American made no mistake as he fired inside the near post to make it 2-0.

Right on the half-hour mark, Genoa thought they had got themselves back into the game when Osmajic headed past Maignan having escaped his man to be found by Vitinha’s flick-on. However, the offside flag was raised and the decision was upheld, though it looked very close.

Despite being two goals up, Milan never gave the impression of being in control and Genoa had a couple of half-chances towards the end of the half, including an Ostigard header that Maignan managed to claim.

The start to the second half was certainly a fractious one, and the Milan players were surrounding the referee Davide Massa five minutes into it when Rabiot seized on a loose touch from Marcandalli to run in behind.

He was dragged back by the defender who appeared to be the last man, but a yellow card was deemed to be sufficient. Rabiot got a yellow too for his protests, and three members of the Milan coaching staff were shown a red.

Amorim opted to make a couple of changes on the hour mark, with Cisse making way for Omari Hutchinson and Diawara coming off for Filippo Terracciano.

As the game entered the final 20 minutes, Milan began to look comfortable with their lead but at times complacent too. Musah gave possession away in the left-back position and it gave Vitinha a dangerous position to get a shot off, though Maignan did well to parry it away.

The pressure continued to come from the Rossoblu, and El Shaarawy had a chance off the bench when a cross found him in the box. He brought it down well, but Terracciano got a knee to it to deflect it over. Pulisic made way for Ardon Jashari after.

Inside the final few minutes Pervis Estupinan became the last player to come, replacing Musah. The sub was made just before El Shaarawy lined up a free-kick from about 22 yards out, and it would yield Genoa’s route back into the game.

The initial shot was blocked as it went into a crowd but was not cleared, allowing Ellertsson all the time in the world to step up and strike one from distance that nestled inside the right post with Maignan rooted. Game on with two minutes of normal time left.

#1819. When will Mauricio Pochettino start work at Manchester United? Delay explained after ‘formal contact’

Manchester United have reached a verbal agreement with Mauricio Pochettino, though he will not start work straight away.

Pochettino emerged as the leading candidate to replace Michael Carrick as manager after Sunday’s 4-4 draw against Aston Villa left the former midfielder on the brink, with Man United sitting in the Premier League relegation zone heading into the international break.

The latest reporting is that while Carrick is due to take Man Utd training on Thursday, as he did on both Tuesday and Wednesday, as per the Athletic, the expectation is he will be relieved of his duties at Old Trafford imminently.

Man United CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are due to return from meetings in Monaco with minority co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and will then inform Carrick of the decision to dismiss him face-to-face.

In the meantime, United are said to have stepped up their pursuit of Pochettino.

It has been widely reported that United have made formal contact with U.S. Soccer, as they look to appoint the United States Men’s National Team (USMNT) boss as their next head coach.

This development comes following reports overnight that Pochettino’s representatives spent Tuesday discussing personal terms with club officials.

As the Argentine signed an extension with U.S. Soccer as recently as August to continue in his role as national team manager, United are required to activate the $10million (£7.4million), release clause in the 54-year-old’s contract.

However, while United are now looking to finalise an agreement with both Pochettino and U.S. Soccer to make him Carrick’s successor, there is a further complication.

Pochettino is currently with the USMNT ahead of the CONCACAF Nations League two-legged quarter-final against Haiti over the next week, and the expectation is that he is likely to remain in charge of those matches before reporting to Carrington.

It is understood that Man United are comfortable with this scenario, though they do run the risk of Pochettino not having much preparation time ahead of the Premier League showdown with Liverpool at Anfield on November 22.

#1818. Chelsea transfer news: Blues face PSG for yougster Kyllian Antonio as RC Lens set asking price

By Axel Clody | 10 Nov 2026 11:50

Chelsea are reportedly among the clubs showing interest in Lens teenager Kyllian Antonio, with Paris Saint-Germain and Aston Villa also watching the defender. Lens have already set a significant asking price for the young player.

Used a handful of times in the first team over the last two seasons, Antonio has fully established himself in the side at the start of the new campaign. The 18-year-old centre-back, who has played 12 matches, nine of them as a starter, is a genuine revelation.

According to Fussball-News, Chelsea, PSG and Aston Villa are following the young defender’s progress closely and are very interested in his potential. PSG’s interest in Antonio is not new, as Lens beat Paris and other French clubs to his signature in the summer of 2023.

He ultimately chose to join the northern club on a free transfer. Lens have done a good piece of business, as the Champigny-sur-Marne native is blossoming and already has a market value of £8.5m (€10m).

Chelsea, PSG and Aston Villa are reportedly considering a move for Antonio and could make their move as early as this winter.

In any case, if one of these suitors makes a move, Lens would expect a fee well above his market value.

The same source reveals that the French club would demand at least £25.5m (€30m) to consider a departure for their gem, who is under contract until June 2028.

It is a figure consistent with Antonio’s potential, but Lens are not really in a position of strength on this one, as the defender will enter the final year of his contract next summer.

To keep the 18-year-old for as long as possible and hope to get the best price for him, Lens will have to extend his contract. However, nothing has emerged on that front for the moment.

#1817. New Bromley boss Karl Robinson heaps praise on 'megastar' Jermain Defoe - with Premier League legend in talks over dugout return after walking out on Woking

Published: 08:00 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 13:33 EST, 7 November 2026

New Bromley boss Karl Robinson has hailed Premier League 'megastar' Jermain Defoe as the ultimate professional following his abrupt departure from Woking.

Daily Mail Sport revealed on Tuesday that Defoe is in talks to join Robinson's backroom staff at League One strugglers Bromley after Andy Woodman's dismissal last month.

And while his appointment has yet to be confirmed, Robinson jumped at the chance to wax lyrical about Defoe at his inauguration on Thursday.

Bromley sit bottom of League One but their new boss believes Defoe's meticulous attention to detail would help the players find another gear.

'There's been a lot of talk but there always is with names like Jermain Defoe, who is a megastar. He's one of the greatest Premier League strikers of all time,' Robinson said.

'I have to raise and change the narrative of what this stands for,' the new boss pointed to the Bromley badge on his jumper.

Jermain Defoe is in talks to join League One strugglers Bromley as Karl Robinson's assistant

Former Salford City manager Robinson has hailed 'megastar' Defoe as the ultimate professional

'I have to bring people in to make me the best version of myself. I spoke to people who know Jermain and played with him.

'He was always first in. All the players who have played with him will tell you that. Steven Gerrard will tell you that.

'He was first in and still in the training ground at 4pm - massages, recovery, gym, video analysis of the players he's playing against.

'I was speaking to him about something completely different the other day and we were talking about discipline and professionalism.

'I said to him: "what do you do that for?". He went: "If I do everything right Monday to Friday and I play poorly, I can accept it because I've done everything in the week to be the best version of myself."

'I'm listening and I've got goose pimples on my arm. Then I'm thinking, that's probably why you're Jermain Defoe, because he did everything he possibly could to maximise his talent.

Defoe has been out of work since walking away from National League side Woking after just four months at the helm amid a strained relationship with the club's director of football.

The 44-year-old took charge of the final six games of last season and was expected to lead the club into the new campaign.

However, he failed to report for work on the eve of the season before contacting the club later that day to inform them he would not be returning.

The former England international and Tottenham Hotspur striker would add top-level experience to the dressing room, having scored 163 Premier League goals in 496 appearances - ranking 10th on the Premier League's scoring charts.

Robinson spoke as though he idolised Defoe when quizzed on his potential appointment, highlighting his humility and relentlessness as key assets to succeed as a coach.

'Failure isn't falling short, it's when you don't maximise your talent. And I think some of the players here haven't maximised their athletic, technical and tactical capabilities', Robinson added.

'For whatever reason, we need to find the key to what that is. I think someone like Jermain (would bring that) because he maximised everything he was and everything he is.

'That's almost the secret behind the genius of the top players. It's their attention to detail, professionalism and discipline – he does that over and over again.

'He's tried to manage in non-league as well. That, in itself, is dropping your ego to learn.'

Although Bromley are still working on finalising Defoe's appointment, he is expected to join Robinson in the dugout at Hayes Lane. The Ravens host Rotherham in the first round of the FA Cup this weekend as Robinson takes his first game in charge.

#1815. Player Ratings: Genoa 1-2 AC Milan – De Winter, Pulisic and Rabiot take charge

AC Milan responded to the criticism with an important win at Genoa on Sunday afternoon. A few players made the difference and below are the ratings for the Rossoneri.

After the mid-week failure against Ferencvaros, Milan knew that three points were more or less a must against Genoa. Thankfully, aside from a dramatic ending, it was a comfortable game for the Rossoneri and a few of the players also got to send some strong signals.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

If you haven’t already, make sure to check out how we decide the player ratings. From the scale to what affects the rating, we have compiled everything there.

🥇 Pulisic (7.5 – MOTM): He did really well to keep his composure after receiving the ball from Ramos, making things comfortable with a two-goal lead. He was also the man who won back the ball before the first goal. In addition to the goals, it felt like he was always available and definitely helped Milan keep possession.

👎 Hutchinson (5.5): He was the worst for me, as he didn’t really add anything in attack and also failed to run down the clock at the end. It’s a shame because there was space to exploit when Genoa pushed forward.

👔 Amorim (6): Fielding Musah on the left actually worked out well, so kudos for that one. The rest of the eleven pretty much picked itself and tactically, while it was a good game, it wasn’t anything extraordinary. But his pre-match message seemed to work, as the players showed more desire.

Maignan (6.5): We saw a couple of good stops from him, including one on Vitinha in the second half, and his distribution was decent. He couldn’t really do anything about the goal either, as it was a really good effort from Ellertsson.

Gila (6): I liked his performance overall but there were a couple of moments that dragged down the rating for me, more specifically the fouls he committed. Put simply, he was a bit too rash and it was after one of the free-kicks he caused that Genoa scored their goal.

De Winter (7.5): The only poor moment came inside the first 60 seconds, when he was caught out a bit by a ball over the top, but he managed to track back and at least narrow the angle. After that, he was brilliant in his positioning, showing off with some great tackles and interceptions too. Really good.

Diawara (6): He was carded for a very rash challenge, but apart from that, he kept his calm at the back and had decent positioning throughout. It’s not like Genoa threatened Milan a lot, but enough for a pass here still.

Moreira (6.5): It was a lively start from him, I would say, with some good moments on that right flank. However, the end product wasn’t always amazing (some blocked shots), and he faded a bit attacking-wise as the game went on. Solid though and he did put in a defensive shift at the end.

Modric (7): We got to see some really nice flicks and quick play from him today. Defensively, he contributed as well, which was especially clear with a last-ditch toe-poke to avoid a 1v1 for Genoa. There was one poor pass into the middle which could have proved costly, but the rest was good.

Rabiot (7.5): He was back to his usual self today after what was a subpar display against Ferencvaros. Great movement between the lines and elegance on the ball were his main strengths, also getting the assist for the opener.

Musah (6): We have to praise him for doing well in a ‘new’ position, following the instructions from Amorim nearly perfectly. What stopped him from getting a higher rating here was the big giveaway at the end, which Genoa really should have done more with.

Pulisic (7.5 – MOTM): He did really well to keep his composure after receiving the ball from Ramos, making things comfortable with a two-goal lead. He was also the man who won back the ball before the first goal. In addition to the goals, it felt like he was always available and definitely helped Milan keep possession.

Cisse (7): It was a very tidy finish to give Milan the lead, showing once again that he knows how to turn up in the right place at the right time. However, for a higher rating, I would have liked to see more in his 1v1s, which weren’t always so successful.

Ramos (5.5): I’m torn here. It was unselfish to pass to Pulisic for the second goal rather than shooting himself, so that deserves praise. However, I actually think he was very sloppy in open play with heavy touches and positioning that sometimes left a lot to be desired. I suppose the big question is how much his defensive work rate is worth to the rating.

Terracciano (6): Surprisingly good! He had a crucial deflection on a shot from El Shaarawy and also headed the ball away quite a few times in the end, certainly contributing to the three points.

Hutchinson (5.5): He was the worst for me, as he didn’t really add anything in attack and also failed to run down the clock at the end. It’s a shame because there was space to exploit when Genoa pushed forward.

Jashari (6): We didn’t see much in terms of attacking contributions and build-up, since he came on with ten minutes to go, but he was responsible for a few clearances at the end.

Estupinan (5.5): I don’t think it was much of a foul, but in those moments, you shouldn’t even give the referee the opportunity to blow the whistle. He knows that.

Amorim (6): Fielding Musah on the left actually worked out well, so kudos for that one. The rest of the eleven pretty much picked itself and tactically, while it was a good game, it wasn’t anything extraordinary. But his pre-match message seemed to work, as the players showed more desire.

#1814. Alexander Isak starts to justify £125m price tag with double

There was a centre-forward who played for Newcastle a couple of years ago. Do you remember him? He was as quick as greased lightning, played on his instincts, had a shot like cannon and could come up with a finish for every situation.

Everyone wanted him, but Liverpool signed him for £125m in August 2025. His name was Alexander Isak but shortly after arriving on Merseyside, it was like he went missing, as the guy who played in red last season bore only a physical resemblance to the guy who had played in black-and-white.

If you had wondered what had happened to him, he reappeared at Portman Road. They say good things come to those who wait. Although nobody at Liverpool would have expected such a delay to see the real Isak, there were no complaints that his career at the club has finally taken off.

Taking the headlines from Bradley Barcola on a big night at Portman Road was going to take some doing, but Isak did just that with a double salvo in the opening nine minutes, a flurry so potent it was like a boxer charging out of their corner and seeing the first blows land flush on their opponent’s jaw.

Poor Ipswich. There is universal recognition that Liverpool are a team – and a club – in transition but they had four players in Isak, Florian Wirtz, Cody Gakpo and Victor Muñoz who had the potential to dismantle the hosts if they clicked and that is precisely what happened.

“With Alex, it is clear,” said Andoni Iraola. “If he is fit, if he is available, if he is in a good shape, he will produce the numbers. My demand with Alex will not be about the goals. It will be about other things so we can play well. And if we play well, we are in good positions. Then goals will come.”

So for all the noisy backing they received from the stands and for all the effort Gary O’Neil’s side put into a contest that TV companies had chosen to broadcast because there was a potential for drama, Isak blew a hole in Ipswich’s hull in the sixth minute and they were submerging from there on in.

A blistering finish from Alexander Isak! 💥 pic.twitter.com/jSGlIZsQtA

How Isak, who had scored against Nottingham Forest last weekend, needed a night like this when he made a genuine difference. But the same was true, too, for Iraola. We live in an era where someone has to be in the eye of a storm and the Basque will know what comes with his new territory.

It had clearly irritated Iraola that Liverpool had gone behind four times in their opening two fixtures and during his pre-match media briefing, he effectively gave a sermon at one point on how slow starts, or giving the opposition a helping hand, would no longer be tolerated.

Quietly, Iraola is making his presence felt. The task he faces is significantly different than the one O’Neil is accomplishing – keeping Ipswich in the division against the odds – but Liverpool’s head coach is a man who knows his own mind and is not afraid to make decisions.

He had responded to criticism of his midfield at Newcastle on the opening weekend by dropping Ryan Gravenberch for the fixture with Forest and his response to scrutiny about his right-back seven days ago was to drop Jeremie Frimpong and bring in Ronald Araújo.

Iraola certainly picked the right team: Araújo, the loan capture from Barcelona, added stature to the back four and there was harmony in how they moved. The Uruguayan’s first instinct was to stay back and Liverpool looked better for it, even if O’Neil, incredibly, felt Ipswich had the better of things.

Emersonn, Ipswich’s Brazilian striker, did not see the ball in the opening exchanges and, by the time he did, Liverpool had zoomed into the distance to such an extent that you felt it was going to be impossible for them to peg their visitors back.

“I hate having to talk about good performances when you do not get points,” O’Neil declared to a room full of raised eyebrows and you can only assume his message was to ensure that morale in the dressing room was not drooping.

What damage was inflicted with Liverpool’s first significant attack. Gakpo, the subject of an £80m bid from Manchester City, was never going to allow transfer speculation to disrupt his focus and he nudged a perfect little ball into Isak’s path in the sixth minute to show his wellbeing.

The next move announced the return of Isak. One touch gave him an avenue to shoot, the next was a shot with his right foot that was so hard from 16 yards, on an angle, it bent the wrists of Kjell Scherpen as it howled into the net. Critics will feel Ipswich’s keeper should have done better.

Your first thought was to think of the first goal Isak scored in English football in September 2022, a similarly venomous drive, against Liverpool at Anfield. He oozed quality that evening, his pace and skill had Jürgen Klopp’s defenders persistently fretting and this is what he was doing again.

It was no coincidence that three minutes later, he came up with another wonderful goal. This one owed much to the beautiful pass Gakpo presented to him, an inch-perfect through ball with the outside of his right foot, but Isak still showed great poise to bamboozle Scherpen.

Inside NINE minutes Alexander Isak has two goals! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/3UGq0bwqRm

“He owes me a few assists now!” chirped the selfless Gakpo.

A hat-trick could have arrived in the 32nd minute but Isak was a kneecap offside as he dispatched a pass from Wirtz and, perhaps, he will have been disappointed to have made way on the hour having not secured the match ball for his efforts.

Liverpool, too, will be frustrated that they did not made sure of three points before the time Isak made way for Barcola – what Alexis Mac Alliser was thinking when he fluffed an unmarked header from six yards, only he will know – but it was not a night to nitpick.

There will be easier assignments on the horizon for Ipswich, even though O’Neil insisted they more than held their own against world-class opponents. And you can say for sure there will be more goals and wins for Liverpool and Isak if they continue in this encouraging manner.

“I witnessed what a great coach he was at Bournemouth. He is not the sort of manager you are going to see making clever patterns in his box. He just does not see the risk. He will want to get the ball to the players who want to make a difference. Coaches do not show how good they are by how they play out from the back. The important thing is when you get it in the final third, you make things happen. That is what he will want to improve. He will want Alexander Isak when he has not got the ball to press. He will want the same of Florian Wirtz. The difficulty will come with Champions League football and not putting too many demands on his players. If he gets it right, he has got a wonderful squad to work with.”

"My demands will not be about the goals, my fights with him are about other stuff." Andoni Iraola speaking about Alexander Isak 🔊 pic.twitter.com/B4zUG2IGfS

“He has had good minutes, a good pass in a counter, a good couple of chances when he was going against the goalkeeper and we have not found him. We need to learn these movements because he will be there threatening in behind all the team. But he looks confident on the ball as always. He had not played any competitive minutes since the World Cup so we had to be a little bit more careful.”

"Yeah, that's nice" 😁Alexander Isak talks through his second goal vs Ipswich 🔍 pic.twitter.com/diG2xv50Bw

“We were waiting for the first win, and we were talking about starting the game well, which we have not done recently. And we did that with two goals. The Swede’s two early goals have earned Liverpool all three points at Portman Road and the travelling Liverpool fans are singing his name. Isak’s fellow teammates are pushing him towards the travelling fans to take their adulation as they belt out his name.

The final whistle goes at Portman Road and Andoni Iraola picks up his first win as Liverpool boss with a 2-0 victory thanks to Isak’s quickfire double inside the opening 10 minutes. Like they did two seasons ago, Liverpool win 2-0 at Portman Road.

Barcola’s first few touches in a Liverpool shirt are pretty good down the left. He is playing in his most natural position of wide left, with Gakpo now down the middle and Szoboszlai on the right.

Andoni Iraola must be ripping his air out with the lack of composure and control from his side since half-time. It is no wonder he is about to turn to his bench and a certain Frenchman.

Enciso is given far too much space to drive towards the Liverpool box before shooting but Alisson makes the save. Liverpool, despite being 2-0 up, have showed a real lack of composure since the break.

If trends are anything to go by, Bradley Barcola will be introduced in the next three or four minutes. Andoni Iraola likes to change things around the hour mark and if the Frenchman warms up anymore, he will nearly overheat.

Kerkez is the latest player into the book for a foul on Fatawu.

Fatawu receives it out on the right for Ipswich and cuts inside onto his preferred left foot before curling an effort towards the far post but it goes wide.

Jacquet takes a heavy touch from a high ball and ends up taking out Emersonn, which earns the Frenchman a booking.

Liverpool work it well down their left as Isak plays it into Gakpo, who drives towards the Ipswich box. He plays it across the face of the penalty area to Szboszblai, who flicks it first time into the path of Wirtz. The German’s effort takes a deflection and goes behind for a corner.

Szoboszlai’s outswinger finds a free Mac Allister at the front post but the Argentine’s header is straight at Scherpen. That was a good chance for Mac Allister.

We are back under way at Portman Road. No changes for either side at the break.

Perhaps if Liverpool were playing a team with a bit more savvy, the 2-0 scoreline they currently protect would have been in jeopardy. Ipswich have put some nice moves together and had half chances but not enough to really turn the screw. Andoni Iraola, certainly, has been unhappy at times and it is becoming a trademark to see him spin around from the technical area in disgust when a ball has been squandered. In the main, though, he can be satisfied with this opening 45 minutes. Liverpool should be winning from here.

The first half is brought to an end at Portman Road and Isak’s quickfire double early in the half gives Liverpool a 2-0 lead at the break.

Wirtz feeds a lovely pass into the left channel to pick out the run of Isak into the Ipswich box but Diop comes in with a crucial challenge.

Two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Araujo slices a clearance out of play for an Ipswich corner. A real gift for the home side as Araujo was not under any real pressure.

Isak should head away at the near post but it comes to Mac Allister to clear away.

A chance for Wirtz as the ball falls to the German on the edge of the Ipswich box but his shot is saved by Scherpen down to his left.

Enciso is the first Ipswich player into the book tonight for delaying a restart.

Szoboszlai, for the third time in the half, shoots from range. Again, the Hungarian gets plenty of power on it but fortunately for Scherpen it is straight at him.

Enciso turns neatly not far outside the Liverpool box and then shoots but slices the shot a fair way wide.

Tommy Elphick, a member of Andoni Iraola’s coaching staff, is booked for his protestations. Liverpool are not happy with some of the fouls being given against them and then some that are not given for them, including a clear foul from Emersonn on Van Dijk that was not penalised.

Isak has the ball in the Ipswich net for the third time tonight and thinks he has his hat-trick but the offside flag goes up. It comes from a stunning piece of play from Wirtz down Liverpool’s left, taking up a pocket of space and taking the ball on the turn beautifully. He then spots Isak in space at the far post and picks him out perfectly, with Isak slotting home. However, the offside flag is up and replays prove he was just offside. Could Isak have timed his run just fractionally better and still reached the cross? Probably but it was very close.

Mac Allister receives a pass from Wirtz and, from just outside the box, decides to shoot but his effort goes just over. Scherpen did appear to have it covered anyway.

A crucial intervention from Araujo. Enciso drives down Ipswich’s right after Fatawu’s header, with Mac Allister tracking back. From the right side of the Liverpool box, Enciso’s deflected cross comes towards Maeda at the far post but Araujo makes an important clearance.

Moments later, Davis again meets a Fatawu cross at the far post but his header is off target.

Fatawu’s dangerous cross from the right all the way to the back post finds Davis, who heads back across goal. Emersonn takes a touch with his chest on the edge of the six-yard box before shooting but Jacquet is on hand to make a crucial block. Ipswich though do have their first corner of the game.

Lukic clips it in and Alisson should punch away with ease. However, the ball comes off Gakpo and, very fortunately for Alisson, the ball gets trapped between his own legs and he can gather. Alisson will be a relieved man.

Szoboszlai sends another powerful shot from range towards the goal and forces Scherpen into another decent save. Ipswich are not helping themselves at times by just giving the ball away inside their own half.

Szoboszlai comes close to adding a third for Liverpool. Fatawu inexplicably gives the ball away inside his own half before Mac Allister plays it forward to Szoboszlai, who takes just one touch before firing towards goal. Scherpen gets down well to his right to make the save.

And there he is. You have been waiting 12 months to see the Alexander Isak of Newcastle play for Liverpool but here he is, a confident, instinctive-finishing menace. His first goal was marvellous, his second was a work of art, given the pass from Cody Gakpo, and what a position Liverpool have put themselves in to get their first win under Andoni Iraola. And, while we are at it, Gakpo has made both Liverpool’s goals: what on earth were they doing thinking of selling him to Manchester City?

Isak, on his last trip to Portman Road, scored a hat-trick for Newcastle here in a 4-0 win back in December 2024. He already has two goals to his name tonight inside the opening quarter of an hour.

Emersonn misses from close range for Ipswich but the offside flag goes up against Greaves. It was a bad miss from Emersonn but Greaves, who had delivered the cross for Emersonn, was offside.

The first booking of the game goes the way of Mac Allister, who is booked slightly harshly for a foul on Enciso.

Moments later, Ipswich have their first effort of the game but Fatawu curls over from the edge of the box.

Another fine goal from Isak and Liverpool lead 2-0 not even 10 minutes into this game. It is Gakpo who assists again with a superb pass with the outside of his right foot from halfway into the left channel to pick out the run in behind of Isak. The Swede cuts inside Greaves onto his right before then chopping back onto his left. He then coolly slots home past Scherpen and Liverpool have the dream start.

Isak’s movement is very clever as he drifts off the defender into space. He takes a touch before smashing the ball past Scherpen at his near post. Should Scherpen have saved that? Possibly but Isak did hit that very hard. For the first time this season, Liverpool lead in a Premier League match.

Fatawu swings it in with his left but Alisson punches away.

It has been all Liverpool in these early stages but have yet to have a shot. Ipswich have barely touched the ball thus far.

Szoboszlai’s outswinger is headed away from danger.

Andoni Iraola wondered what might happen when he first sat down to talk with Bradley Barcola.

Here was one of the world’s best wingers, with his 13 major honours, 28 international caps and £123m price tag – a combination that could easily lead a man to view himself through the prism of a superstar: never mind what I can do for you, what can you do for me?

Liverpool’s due diligence on Barcola had all been positive – not least from the currently injured Hugo Ekitike, who had been a vocal advocate of his compatriot’s capabilities to the recruitment team – but Iraola wanted to gauge for himself exactly what the 24-year-old was going to offer.

We are about to find out the two starting XIs at Portman Road. Will Bradley Barcola start for Liverpool on his debut?

The third matchday of the new Premier League season kicks off at Portman Road as newly-promoted Ipswich host Liverpool.

Andoni Iraola has drawn his first two games in charge of Liverpool, both 2-2 stalemates against Newcastle and Nottingham Forest respectively. Liverpool secured a move for forward Bradley Barcola from PSG in the final few days on the window for a fee that could rise to £123m and the Frenchman is set to make his Liverpool debut tonight.

“We are very happy with Bradley,” Iraola said. “He was our priority; to sign a very good player in that position. He has come with the right mentality. I like that he wanted Liverpool a lot, he just wanted to come here. That is a good first sign. Being the player he is and the things he has won recently, he has come with the willingness to help us. I am very happy with him.

“He trained well with us, and if everything goes well in today’s [Thursday] training, he will definitely be available for tomorrow [tonight]. He has trained with us three times. He has not had minutes in pre-season but he has been training normally with the group. It is a decision we have to make. We have to consider that he has not had minutes in pre-season.”

Liverpool won both fixtures when Ipswich were last in the Premier League two seasons ago, including a 2-0 win on the opening weekend in Arne Slot’s first game in charge of Liverpool as they went on to win the Premier League that season.

Ipswich won their first home game on their return to the Premier League, beating Sunderland 2-1 on the opening weekend. However, they fell to a 5-2 defeat in their first away game at Manchester United. Over the course of the summer transfer window, Ipswich made a total of 14 signings and spent over £200m.

“What we can do is perform in a way that always gives us a real chance, which we have done so far,” Ipswich boss Gary O’Neil said. “We were in that game at Manchester United until a couple of moments took it away from us. We were in it, so that is what we need to do, we need to make sure that no matter who it is, whether it is Liverpool, Manchester United, Manchester City, when they come to Portman Road, we need to make sure we are right in the game to give ourselves opportunities. We will always be a threat; we have scored four goals in two games. That is really good for a promoted side. We look a goal threat, and we need to keep that going and that will be tested.”

Team news from Portman Road to follow shortly.

#1813. Sunderland injury news: Granit Xhaka fitness update provides reason for Stadium of Light concern

By Carter White | 10 Nov 2026 11:59

Sunderland midfielder Granit Xhaka has withdrawn from international duty with Switzerland this month.

The 34-year-old started on Sunday afternoon in the top flight for Regis Le Bris's side as an Enzo Le Fee penalty was enough to secure maximum points over Chelsea, however, the Black Cats are still 19th in the Premier League standings.

Xhaka lasted just four minutes of the North-East contest before being replaced, with Sunderland going on to defeat the visiting Blues, who were again without the services of star striker Joao Pedro.

After the opening 10 matches of the Premier League campaign, Le Bris's troops have collected just eight points, sitting only above crisis-hit Crystal Palace in the rankings as a relegation battle looms large.

Sunderland will be looking to record back-to-back top-flight victories for the first time this season following the international pause on November 21, when they make the tricky trip to Aston Villa.

Speaking on social media, the Swiss FA have confirmed that Sunderland midfielder Xhaka has been withdrawn from international duty this month, representing a major blow to both his club and country.

The post reveals that the 34-year-old's problem is a calf issue, with the former Bundesliga champion set to miss UEFA Nations League clashes with Slovenia and Scotland over the next week.

When quizzed on Xhaka's issue following the Chelsea win, Sunderland boss Le Bris said: “It looks like a calf injury, but we do not know exactly the timeframe at the minute. It was just the last sprint of the warm-up, that is often the case [with these injuries].”

The ex-Arsenal man had a scan on his injured calf yesterday with the results yet to be revealed, however, the fitness setback is clearly large enough to keep him sidelined over the next fortnight.

Murat Yakin's Swiss side have enjoyed a marvellous start to their Nations League B campaign, winning four consecutive matches in the September/October window to give themselves the opportunity to secure promotion with a victory in Slovenia on Friday.

After featuring in 99 competitive games for Bayer Leverkusen over a two-year period, Xhaka arrived at the Stadium of Light during the summer of 2025, helping Sunderland to reach new Premier League heights.

The veteran midfielder featured in 36 games across all competitions for the Black Cats as they avoided relegation with ease, instead securing a spot in this season's edition of the Europa League.

In the twilight of his career, it is no surprise that niggling injuries are beginning to hinder Xhaka, who has gone through an enormous amount of midfield work for Leverkusen and Sunderland since 2023.

#1812. Mauricio Pochettino to Manchester United latest: £7.4m clause, verbal agreement and transfer targets

Manchester United headed into the final international break of the year with uncertainty over the managerial position, though the next few days are set to prove crucial.

Michael Carrick was left on the brink following Man Utd’s 4-4 draw at home to Aston Villa at the weekend, a result that leaves the side in the Premier League relegation zone after one win from the opening 10 matches.

In a surprising turn of events, Mauricio Pochettino has emerged as the leading contender to replace Carrick at Old Trafford, and it would appear things is gathering pace for some major announcements in the coming hours and days.

Below is what we know about the Man Utd managerial situation.

According to The Athletic, Pochettino’s representatives spent Tuesday discussing personal terms with Manchester United officials, with no major obstacles expected and a final agreement expected.

It has since been reported that United have reached a verbal agreement in principle with Pochettino to take over as head coach, though the Argentine is likely to remain in charge of USA’s CONCACAF Nations League two-legged quarter-final against Haiti.

The second of those ties is in the early hours on Wednesday, November 18 (UK time) which would not give Pochettino too much time with the Man United squad ahead of the Premier League showdown against Liverpool.

For Man Utd to appoint Pochettino, it will not be a cheap deal. This is because the Argentine signed a new contract with US Soccer in August to continue in his role as USMNT manager.

According to The Athletic, there is a buyout clause in Pochettino’s contract worth $10million (£7.44million) which Man Utd can trigger to bring back him to England.

However, the buyout clause does not cover Pochettino’s coaching staff, many of who - such as assistant Jesus Perez - has been with him most the majority of his career.

Another huge breakthrough came on Wednesday night (November 11) as Manchester United are said to have stepped up their pursuit of Mauricio Pochettino.

According to the Athletic, United have now made formal contact with U.S. Soccer, as they look to appoint the United States Men’s National Team (USMNT) boss as their next head coach.

Michael Carrick took training on Tuesday and Wednesday and, as of writing, officially remains Man United boss.

However, Sky Sports claim he is likely to be relieved of his duties before the end of the week, once CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox have returned from their meeting with co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco which took place on Wednesday.

It is understood that Berrada and Wilcox are likely to recommend to Ratcliffe that a change is made in an attempt to halt United’s alarming run of form that has seen them win just one of their opening 10 Premier League matches.

Furthermore, it’s claimed that Carrick will be informed of the decision to dismiss him face-to-face.

Mauricio Pochettino will run into an immediate problem at Manchester United with the squad is not capable of playing his high-pressing brand of football.

The answer? The transfer market. Pochettino will likely require a complete overhaul, starting in the January window.

Man Utd have attempted to refresh different areas of the squad over the last two summers, spending hundreds of millions on the attack in 2025 before replacing the midfield during the summer just gone.

The defence is crying out for investment, quite literally in the case of Lisandro Martinez, who attacked Man Utd’s hierarchy over a failure to recruit properly during the summer.

Man Utd require new full-backs, frequently playing right-backs on the left and then requiring a centre-half to fill in on the right.

“I think he’s done everything he could for Portugal. It’s his decision, and we have to respect it. I think the entire football world should be happy for him, and I wish him the best for the rest of his career.”

What is your assessment of these nine matches between the international breaks?

“The important thing is that we have to find this consistency, because it’s important, but it’s a process and we have to keep believing in it.”

“I think the coach put me in this position because he knows I can run all the way up and down the flank, and yes, it’s part of my game. I run a lot and I think that helps the team, and I have to continue doing it because, yes, if I can help the team in this way, I will do it every time.”

#1810. Osmand proves he's no Honda Civic... and now he's ready to motor on for Celtic

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 13:00 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 13:48 EST, 7 November 2026

When Brendan Rodgers returns to Glasgow for a Q&A session next June, it would feel like a waste of time for him to be grilled on the exact reasons behind his team selection for matches which, by then, will have taken place almost two years ago.

Frankly, those assembled in the Royal Concert Hall that evening will have their mind on other matters.

Nonetheless, there remains a curiosity about why the Northern Irishman overlooked Callum Osmand at a time when Celtic were evidently crying out for a spark up front.

Rodgers, you may well remember, had spoken with great excitement about the club signing the player from Fulham a few weeks previously.

Sure, Osmand was only 19 at the time. He hadn't played a single minute of first-team football, either.

But as a combination of Daizen Maeda and the soon-to-depart Adam Idah failed to find the net across 210 minutes against Kairat Almaty, you couldn't help but wonder if the much-vaunted teenager stationed on the bench in both legs might have been worth a shot.

Despite Rodgers giving Osmand the big build up that summer, the forward didn't play a single minute prior to his abrupt departure at the end of October.

While that was clearly his prerogative, the impact Osmand has made across an injury-stricken year does suggest that it was an oversight.

Handed his debut as a substitute by Martin O'Neill against Falkirk soon after, Osmand scored a brilliant flashing header in the League Cup semi-final against Rangers before sustaining a serious hamstring tear against Midtjylland.

Only back in contention on the final day of the season after surgery, he set up Maeda and scored himself as Celtic clinched the title in dramatic fashion against Hearts.

Having been sidelined again with an ankle injury at the outset of this campaign, he's rebounded in some style. His goal and assist for Camilo Duran against Besiktas on Thursday came a couple of weeks after scoring twice in a 7-1 rout against the Tynecastle men in what was his first senior start.

Callum Osmand made an instant impression off the bench against Besiktas

After just 13 matches for Celtic, it may be a little too early to describe Osmand as a Ferrari. But a Honda Civic, he is most certainly not.

The beauty of the situation, from the club's perspective, is that the player hasn't even revved the engine as he sets out on his career path.

Osmand, who turns 21 as Kilmarnock visit today, looks first-team ready any time he's taken the field. Yet he's the first to admit that the game-time those injuries denied him stunted his development.

Provided there's a fair wind at his back, though, he's certain there's a lot more to come.

'I would say I'm nowhere near where I want to be personally,' he said.

'There's stuff I need to tidy up on, like decision-making and all this stuff.

'But I feel like the more games I play, the more I understand and the more I learn.

'So, on a personal note, that's what I'd want to do - just keep learning and keep understanding my role within the team and obviously the players you're playing with.

'I've still only played a handful of games, so it's tough learning. But I feel like when you get thrown in the deep end, it's the best way to learn. You learn more off the worst games than the good games.

'It's just as long as I can get better every game, that's all I really want to focus on.'

There's no doubt, though, that there are many moments when he looks the real deal.

For instance, his brilliant finish after Callum McGregor's square ball on Thursday, his first touch after coming off the bench.

'It was crazy,' he smiled. 'It's a surreal feeling when it's my first touch as well.

'I was a bit nervous that I'd shanked it, but no, I'm happy that I caught it nicely.'

One of his next involvements wasn't too bad, either. Motoring into space off the left flank, Osmand had to find the perfect weight and direction on the pass which would allow Camilo Duran to exploit a pocket of space and round the keeper. He could not have played it better.

Osmand has struck up a good understanding with fellow Celtic striker Camilo Duran

'I thought he was offside, to be honest,' he recalled of the moment in which Celtic moved 2-1 in front.

'I was looking at the bench saying 'Close?' and they were like, "Yeah, it's tight".

'But I know where he's going. He's such a sharp striker, so I know if I put that in the space, the keeper is not getting anywhere near it. He's a top, top player, so I can't fault him at all.'

With all due respect to Colby Donovan – also assured after coming off the bench – Thursday night will long be remembered for the belated contributions of Osmand and Duran, who scored three goals between them.

The Colombian began on the right flank, but moved infield once Kasper Hogh tired. The understanding Duran had with Osmand was clear throughout and ultimately proved the undoing of the Turks.

'He's unbelievable, a really top player,' Osmand said. 'You can just see even by the way he walks and the way he moves.

'I learn off him every day. He's an amazing guy. His English is really not great, but somehow we manage to talk to each other a lot.

'I think I find him quite a good friend of mine now.

'And although we might not speak many words, you can tell just by looking ... I don't know how to describe it. Like we talk to each other a lot. Maybe it's little words, but I feel like we get on really well. He's a great guy.'

Duran's finish at the second attempt to seal the victory later on felt hugely significant for all associated with Celtic.

It was precisely the kind of big win at the right moment which O'Neill and his embattled squad needed to blow away the storm clouds. On such moments, entire seasons can hinge and reputations are forged.

'For us, it felt like a must win, like that was our sort of mindset going into that,' Osmand said.

'I think the boys did amazing, so hopefully we just get some confidence and build on from this and that gives us confidence to play more free and take more risks.

'Sometimes when you're not as confident, it's tough to play the football you want to play.'

#1809. Michael Carrick future: Judgment day ‘revealed’ as Jim Ratcliffe receives final Man Utd sack recommendation

By Oliver Thomas | 10 Nov 2026 12:30, Last updated: 10 Nov 2026 12:35

A final decision on Michael Carrick’s future as Manchester United head coach will be made on Wednesday, according to multiple reports.

The 45-year-old appears to be hanging onto his job by the thinnest of threads, with reports emerging on Monday evening claiming that he is expected to be sacked before the Red Devils’ next Premier League game against Liverpool on November 22.

Man United slipped down to 18th in the Premier League table following a chaotic 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday, sparking unimaginable fears of relegation.

Carrick has overseen just one victory in 10 top-flight matches this season, with his team conceding an alarming 19 goals – the joint-third most in the division.

The Red Devils have also lost two of their opening four matches in the Champions League and have penalty of work to do if they wish to avoid an embarrassing League Phase exit.

It is understood that director of football Jason Wilcox is leading the review into Carrick’s future, with chief executive Omar Berrada also being consulted, before a recommendation is made to minority shareholder Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

Both Wilcox and Berrada met at Man United’s Carrington training complex on Monday to hold initial discussions and conduct a full review of the club’s season so far during the international break.

According to multiple reports, including Sky Sports and BBC Sport, Wilcox and Berrada were not present at the club’s training ground on Tuesday, but Carrick was at Carrington as normal.

A meeting in Monaco attended by Ratcliffe, Wilcox and Berrada is said to have been scheduled for Wednesday where the latter two will present their findings to the former over Carrick, with his future looking increasingly doubtful.

This pre-planned meeting between the trio is not an emergency one and has not been organised to strictly discuss Carrick’s future, though that will be one of the key topics of discussion.

The Glazer family – Man United’s majority owners – will also be informed, but a final decision may not be official announced until Thursday.

It is understood that if Man United’s final decision is to sack Carrick, then the club would like to inform him face to face.

It has previously been suggested that former Newcastle United boss Eddie Howe and ex-Germany head coach Julian Nagelsmann were the two leading candidates to replace Carrick.

However, recent reports have since emerged claiming that former Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea manager Mauricio Pochettino is firmly back in the frame having previously been linked with the Old Trafford hotseat before Carrick’s permanent appointment.

Pochettino is currently in charge of the USA national team, but it has been suggested that he would be interested in becoming Man United’s new manager.

The 54-year-old only signed a new four-year contract extension in August taking him through to the 2030 World Cup.

However, his new deal is said to have a release clause worth in the region of £7.4m, a figure that would seemingly tempt Man United to prise him away from his national team job.

Carrick, meanwhile, is under contract at Old Trafford until the summer of 2028, but his deal is believed to include a break clause that would make his dismissal more affordable.

#1808. Tuchel confirms Kane will win record-breaking 126th England cap versus Croatia

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Harry Kane will win his record-breaking 126th England cap against Croatia, Thomas Tuchel has confirmed, with the Three Lions' boss anticipating a "beautiful occasion".

Kane's next England outing will see him write his name into the record books, as he surpasses Peter Shilton (125) outright as his country's all-time leading appearance-maker.

The Bayern Munich striker has long been England's all-time leading scorer, having surpassed Wayne Rooney's record in March 2023, reaching 91 international goals since then.

And Kane's landmark appearance will come on home soil at Wembley Stadium on Thursday, on the same night that he presents the Ballon d'Or trophy to the Three Lions' fans, having been crowned the world's best player last month.

Asked by reporters if Kane was England's greatest-ever player, Tuchel said: "I don't know, but he is up there, of course. It's now proven, and it's nice when things are proven in sports.

"He has his collection of prizes, he has his records, and he will build on these records, he will score more goals for us and get more games.

"Tomorrow, he will start for us, of course. He will start as the captain and it will be a big occasion, to present the Ballon d'Or trophy, to bring it to the country.

"And to have that embedded in the same day where he gets his all-time record… it will be a beautiful occasion."

“A beautiful, beautiful occasion.”  #ThreeLions skipper @HKane is set to make history at @wembleystadium  https://t.co/pqH91IidZ7

Kane has scored 13 goals for England in 2026, with only Kane himself in 2021 scoring more in a single calendar year for the Three Lions (16).

Four of those goals came as braces against Croatia (two in June, two in October) with no England player ever scoring multiple goals in three straight games against a single opponent.

Kane has also netted braces in his last two appearances for England overall (versus Croatia and Czechia), meaning he could become the first player since Wayne Rooney, in March 2009, to net two or more goals in three consecutive games for the Three Lions.

But Tuchel feels Kane's playmaking ability is what sets him apart from every other striker on the planet.

Asked if any other player could do what Kane does, Tuchel said: "Maybe not at the moment. Everyone plays differently.

"On the very highest level, Lionel Messi developed a completely new style of number nine at Barcelona and dropped everywhere.

"But he was more of a dribbler and accelerator from these spaces, Harry is more a passer and an accelerator through his passing range.

"Everyone is different. Harry is quite unique in the way he does it. That's not the only thing; he's also in and around the box, and you still want the ball to drop to him if it's a one or two-touch finish. He's the one who is clinical and finishes on the very highest level.

"That's why he got the biggest individual award in the game, because he's a unique player at the moment."

England only need a point against Croatia to secure their place in the Nations League quarter-finals, and they could still top Group A3, with a trip to Spain to come on Sunday.
